articles.title: Ações da Nvidia despencam após investigação sobre suspeita de espionagem envolvendo CEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Papéis da fabricante de chips caíam mais de 4% antes da abertura da bolsa de Nova York, após investigação levantar suspeitas de ligação entre Jensen Huang e uma suposta agente da inteligência chinesa.
articles.summary: Ações da Nvidia caíam mais de 4% antes da abertura da bolsa de Nova York, após investigação sobre suposta ligação do CEO Jensen Huang com uma agente da inteligência chinesa.
articles.body:
As ações da Nvidia caíam 4,50% nesta segunda-feira (9), negociadas a US$ 178,25 (cerca de R$ 983) por volta das 12h08 (horário de Brasília), após a abertura da bolsa de Nova York.

A queda ocorre após a abertura de uma investigação interna para apurar se o presidente-executivo da empresa, Jensen Huang, havia sido alvo de uma operação de espionagem estrangeira , levantando dúvidas sobre sua permanência no comando da fabricante de chips de inteligência artificial (IA).

A investigação foi iniciada após uma reportagem apontar que Huang mantinha um relacionamento próximo com uma empresária chinesa suspeita de repassar informações ao governo de Pequim.

O executivo admitiu aos funcionários da Nvidia que havia traído a esposa, mas não revelou detalhes sobre o relacionamento.

Anunciada no domingo (8), a investigação levantou questionamentos sobre o futuro de Huang à frente da Nvidia , a fabricante de chips mais valiosa do mundo.

O executivo também é uma das principais figuras responsáveis pelo crescimento do setor de inteligência artificial.

Os efeitos da investigação chegaram à Coreia do Sul, onde Madison Huang, filha do executivo e também funcionária da Nvidia , cancelou uma viagem a Seul.

Ela participaria de uma conferência da empresa, prevista para começar nesta segunda-feira, segundo companhias com as quais tinha reuniões agendadas.

Na bolsa de Frankfurt, as ações da Nvidia chegaram a cair mais de 6%, ampliando as perdas registradas na semana passada e atingindo os menores níveis em vários meses.

Com essa desvalorização, a empresa corria o risco de perder cerca de US$ 270 bilhões (R$ 1,49 trilhão) em valor de mercado em relação ao fechamento de sexta-feira (6), segundo dados da LSEG Datastream.

"O mercado provavelmente está sinalizando que isso não ajuda em nada as ações, em um momento em que há muitas especulações sobre a expansão dos centros de processamento de dados", afirmou Chris Weston, chefe de pesquisa da corretora Pepperstone, em Melbourne.

Apesar da reação negativa dos investidores, Weston disse não acreditar que Huang, a quem chamou de "padrinho da IA", seja substituído.

"Se realmente acreditássemos que ele deixaria o cargo, as ações estariam despencando. Seria um verdadeiro banho de sangue, para ser sincero", afirmou.

O jornal The New York Times noticiou, no mês passado, que Huang mantinha um relacionamento com Alice Huang, ex-executiva da Megaspeed, empresa sediada em Cingapura.

Apesar do sobrenome, os dois não têm parentesco. Segundo a reportagem, autoridades americanas investigaram Alice e concluíram que ela atuava como agente da inteligência chinesa.

"A chamada narrativa da espionagem chinesa é puramente uma acusação infundada, calúnia e difamação", afirmou o porta-voz do Ministério das Relações Exteriores da China, Guo Jiakun, a jornalistas em Pequim.

A Megaspeed não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário nesta segunda-feira, feriado em Cingapura.

Alice Huang também não respondeu ao New York Times quando o jornal revelou o relacionamento, no mês passado.

A Reuters tentou localizá-la nesta segunda-feira para pedir um posicionamento, mas não conseguiu contato.

Fornecedores asiáticos não foram afetados

Jensen Huang, CEO da Nvidia, durante evento em Washington — Foto: Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo

As ações dos principais fornecedores asiáticos de chips da Nvidia — TSMC, Samsung Electronics e SK Hynix — se recuperaram nesta segunda-feira, após as quedas registradas na semana passada entre empresas ligadas à inteligência artificial.

Os papéis da TSMC subiram 6,5%, enquanto os da Samsung e da SK Hynix avançaram 2,9% e 4,7%, respectivamente.

A confissão de Huang também provocou reações de empresários e investidores.

O bilionário Bill Ackman, fundador da Pershing Square Capital Management, afirmou na rede social X que o presidente-executivo da Nvidia é um "ser humano incrível", mas ressaltou que, se o episódio envolver algo além de uma traição, o caso será grave.

"Espero que seja apenas um caso amoroso, e não um risco à nossa segurança nacional", acrescentou.

O presidente-executivo da Tesla, Elon Musk , também se manifestou. Ele escreveu "Concordo" em uma publicação de Shaun Maguire, sócio da empresa de investimentos Sequoia, que classificou a atitude de Huang como "incrivelmente idiota" e prejudicial aos Estados Unidos.

Apesar das críticas, Maguire afirmou que o executivo é "insubstituível para a liderança dos Estados Unidos em IA".

O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump , afirmou no domingo que ainda não havia conversado com Huang sobre as acusações, mas elogiou o executivo. "Espero que esteja tudo bem. Ele fez um trabalho incrível", declarou.

Questionado se deveria ter tomado alguma providência ao receber informações dos serviços de inteligência sobre o caso, Trump respondeu: "Não, não acho. Acho que ele é um cara honrado. Acho que provavelmente tem uma justificativa para isso. É preciso ouvir o que ele tem a dizer."

Segundo o New York Times, Trump foi informado sobre as conclusões dos serviços de inteligência há cerca de um ano, mas decidiu não tomar nenhuma medida.

articles.title: PIX bate recorde com 319,7 milhões de transações em um único dia | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo o Banco Central, essas operações em PIX movimentaram R$ 180,5 bilhões. Números foram registrados na última sexta-feira (6) e divulgados nesta segunda (9).
articles.summary: PIX bate recorde de transações com 319,7 milhões de operações em um dia, somando R$ 180,5 bilhões, enquanto o Banco Central anuncia novas medidas de segurança.
articles.body:
O Banco Central (BC) informou, nesta segunda-feira (9), que o volume diário de transações feitas pelo PIX atingiu novo recorde na última sexta-feira (6), quando foram registradas 319,7 milhões de transações em um único dia.

Segundo o BC, essas operações em PIX movimentaram R$ 180,5 bilhões .

🔎Segundo a autoridade monetária, o recorde anterior foi alcançado em 4 de setembro deste ano, quando foram registradas 318,1 milhões de transações.

O PIX, sistema de pagamentos instantâneos do Banco Central do Brasil (BC), completa seis anos neste mês.

De acordo com o BC, o resultado "é mais uma demonstração da importância do PIX como infraestrutura digital pública, para o funcionamento da economia nacional".

Entre as principais novidades, os aplicativos de bancos e instituições financeiras passarão a permitir que o cliente anexe documentos e comprovantes no momento de contestar uma transferência fraudulenta, facilitando a identificação dos criminosos e a análise dos casos.

As alterações estão na versão 7.4 do Manual de Requisitos Mínimos para a Experiência do Usuário do PIX. Segundo o BC, as novas regras entrarão em vigor no dia 1º de março de 2027, prazo definido para que as instituições adequem os sistemas e interfaces de seus aplicativos.

articles.title: Caixa muda identidade visual pela primeira vez em quase 30 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Banco mantém o tradicional X e as cores azul e laranja, mas reformula o logotipo; identidade visual será implementada gradualmente nas agências até 2030
articles.summary: Banco mantém o tradicional X e as cores azul e laranja, mas reformula o logotipo; identidade visual será implementada gradualmente nas agências até 2030
articles.body:
A Caixa Econômica Federal lançou nesta segunda-feira (9) uma nova identidade visual, a primeira grande reformulação da marca em quase 30 anos.

A mudança preserva elementos tradicionais, como o nome Caixa, o X e as cores azul e laranja, mas altera o desenho do logotipo e a apresentação visual do banco.

Uma das principais mudanças está no logotipo. O nome Caixa passa a ter letras com a mesma altura, combinando caracteres maiúsculos e minúsculos. O X, símbolo que ganhou destaque na identidade visual do banco em 1997, também foi redesenhado, mas continua como elemento central da marca.

As cores azul e laranja foram mantidas, mas ganharam tonalidades mais vibrantes. A instituição também criou novos grafismos a partir do X, que poderão ser utilizados em diferentes materiais e ambientes digitais.

A nova identidade já foi aplicada em 11 agências distribuídas pelas cinco regiões do país. Entre elas está a unidade do Conjunto Nacional, na Avenida Paulista, em São Paulo, que será reaberta ao público em 11 de novembro.

A atualização visual será implementada gradualmente nas demais unidades, acompanhando obras de modernização e manutenção. A previsão da Caixa é concluir o processo até 2030.

articles.title: Governo prorroga desoneração da gasolina e do etanol por mais 30 dias | G1
articles.standfirst: Decreto prorroga desoneração dos tributos federais sobre a gasolina e etanol e mantém a subvenção adicional aos produtores de etanol. Medidas vão valer até 9 de dezembro.
articles.summary: Decreto prorroga desoneração dos tributos federais sobre a gasolina e etanol e mantém a subvenção adicional aos produtores de etanol. Medidas vão valer até 9 de dezembro.
articles.body:
O governo federal prorrogou por mais 30 dias a desoneração dos tributos federais sobre a gasolina e o etanol. A medida também prevê a manutenção da subvenção adicional aos produtores de etanol.

A medida foi publicada em edição extra do Diário Oficial da União (DOU).

Com a prorrogação, as medidas seguem em vigor até 9 de dezembro.

A desoneração aos combustíveis foi anunciada em 9 de outubro , 16 dias antes do segundo turno das eleições, junto com uma série de medidas para conter o preço dos combustíveis.

À época, o ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, afirmou que, embora as medidas tenham sido anunciadas em meio ao período eleitoral, as decisões do governo não têm relação com a disputa presidencial.

As medidas têm o objetivo de evitar uma alta nos preços dos combustíveis, amenizando os efeitos da elevação do preço do petróleo em decorrência dos conflitos no Oriente Médio. Diante disso, o governo anunciou no mês passado:

Gasolina : decreto que zera os tributos federais (PIS/Pasep, Cofins e CIDE-Combustíveis) incidentes sobre a importação e comercialização de gasolina. A redução anterior de R$ 0,63 foi ampliada, alcançando um corte total de R$ 0,89 por litro. O custo total por mês passou R$ 2,4 bilhões, uma elevação de R$ 700 milhões.

Etanol : foi prorrogada a desoneração do etanol hidratado em R$ 0,19 por litro, e a subvenção econômica aos produtores e cooperativas subiu de R$ 0,25 para R$ 0,43 por litro. O impacto fiscal combinado das medidas para gasolina e etanol é estimado em R$ 3,6 bilhões para 2026, com compensação garantida por receitas extraordinárias de petróleo da União.

Diesel : concessão de uma subvenção adicional aos importadores de óleo diesel rodoviário de R$ 1,40 por litro, valor que se soma aos R$ 2,12 por litro já vigentes, por um período de 30 dias, totalizando um custo estimado de R$ 1,6 bilhão para assegurar a continuidade das importações e o abastecimento do país.

articles.title: Mercado eleva estimativa de inflação para 2027 e passa a prever corte de juros só em março do ano que vem | G1
articles.standfirst: Expectativas são divulgadas toda semana pelo Banco Central (BC), com base em pesquisa realizada com mais de 100 instituições financeiras. Recorte de agora faz referência à semana passada.
articles.summary: Expectativas são divulgadas toda semana pelo Banco Central (BC), com base em pesquisa realizada com mais de 100 instituições financeiras. Recorte de agora faz referência à semana passada.
articles.body:
Os economistas do mercado financeiro elevaram a estimativa de inflação em 2027 e passaram a projetar um novo corte na taxa básica de juros da economia somente em março do próximo ano.

A mudança na aposta do mercado financeiro para a taxa Selic veio após o Comitê de Política Monetária (Copom) ter interrompido, na semana passada, o ciclo de corte nos juros diante da deterioração do cenário econômico com a reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva .

As informações fazem parte do "Boletim Focus", divulgado nesta terça-feira (9) pelo Banco Central (BC), com base em pesquisa realizada na última semana com mais de 100 instituições financeiras.

➡️ Para 2026, a estimativa de inflação permaneceu em 5,22%;

➡️ Para 2027, a expectativa subiu de 4,76% para 4,90%;

➡️ Para 2028, a previsão continuou em 4%;

➡️ Para 2029, a estimativa avançou de 3,98% para 4%.

🔎 Por que isso importa? Quanto maior a inflação, menor é o poder de compra da população — especialmente entre quem recebe salários mais baixos. Isso ocorre porque os preços sobem, enquanto os salários não acompanham esse aumento.

Para o crescimento do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) deste ano, o mercado financeiro reduziu sua estimativa de 1,76% para 1,75% na semana passada.

Com isso, os analistas estimam desaceleração da economia neste ano , visto que, em 2025, o PIB cresceu 2,3% , conforme divulgação oficial do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística ( IBGE ).

➡️ O Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) é a soma de todos os bens e serviços produzidos no país e serve para medir o desempenho da economia.

🔎Se o PIB cresce, significa que a economia vai bem e produz mais. Se o PIB cai, quer dizer que a economia está encolhendo. Entretanto, nem sempre crescimento do PIB equivale a bem-estar social.

Para 2027, a projeção do mercado de crescimento do PIB caiu de 1,20% para 1,15%.

Para 2028, a estimativa do mercado para a expansão da economia permaneceu em 1,80%.

Em um ano eleitoral, o governo adotou ações para estimular a economia e reduzir o endividamento da população, o que impulsiona a demanda por produtos e serviços.

A estratégia do governo, porém, dificultou o controle da inflação. O BC tem dito claramente que uma desaceleração, ou seja, um ritmo menor de crescimento da economia, faz parte da estratégia de conter as pressões inflacionárias.

Após reeleição de Lula, mercado financeiro vê inflação mais alta e piora bastante previsão para taxa de juros e dólar. — Foto: Foto: Rafa Neddermeyer/Agência Brasil

Após a decisão do BC de manter o juro estável em 13,75% ao ano na semana passada, os analistas do mercado financeiro passaram a projetar um novo corte nos juros somente em março do próximo ano — quando a taxa cairia para 13,50% ao ano.

A estimativa do mercado para a taxa Selic ao fim de 2026 subiu de 13,50% para 13,75% ao ano na última semana.

Para o fechamento de 2027, a projeção do mercado permaneceu em 12,5% ao ano.

Para o fim de 2028, a estimativa dos analistas permaneceu em 11% ao ano.

Para o fim de 2029, a expectativa dos analistas continuou em 10,25% ao ano.

O mercado financeiro elevou sua estimativa para a taxa de câmbio ao fim deste ano de R$ 5,34 para R$ 5,35 por dólar.

Para o fechamento de 2027, a projeção dos economistas dos bancos permaneceu em R$ 5,40 por dólar.

Para o fim de 2028, a expectativa do mercado para o dólar passou de R$ 5,40 para R$ 5,45.

Já para o fechamento de 2029, avançou de R$ 5,45 para R$ 5,50 por dólar.

articles.title: Veja o que saiu no primeiro leilão do Master e o que vem no próximo | G1
articles.standfirst: Primeiro leilão, com 445 lotes de móveis, decoração e eletrônicos, foi encerrado nesta segunda-feira (9). Segundo evento terá 258 lotes e será encerrado em 30 de novembro, a partir das 13h30, na plataforma Kwara.
articles.summary: Primeiro leilão, com 445 lotes de móveis, decoração e eletrônicos, foi encerrado nesta segunda-feira (9).
articles.body:
Bens do Banco Master e do Will Bank estão sendo vendidos em dois leilões pela plataforma Kwara , em meio ao processo de liquidação extrajudicial das instituições financeiras .

O primeiro evento , com 445 lotes de móveis, itens de decoração e eletrônicos, foi encerrado nesta segunda-feira (9), às 11h59.

Já o segundo evento, intitulado "Desativação de Banco Master e Will Bank (em Liquidação Extrajudicial) – Itens de Cozinha Industrial", reúne 258 lotes focados em eletrodomésticos . O leilão está aberto até 13h30 do dia 30 de novembro. Para acessar, clique aqui .

Entre os produtos oferecidos nos eventos estão cadeiras de escritório de marcas como Herman Miller e Haworth , televisores , notebooks , máquinas de café , adegas climatizadas , fornos industriais e equipamentos de refrigeração.

Primeiro leilão foi encerrado nesta segunda

O primeiro evento, chamado de "Desativação de Banco Master e Will Bank (em Liquidação Extrajudicial) – Móveis, Decoração e Eletrônicos", reuniu 445 lote s . Os itens foram disponibilizados para lances na plataforma Kwara, e o leilão terminou nesta segunda-feira (9), às 11h59.

Entre os produtos estavam cadeiras de escritório das marcas Herman Miller e Haworth, poltronas, sofás, mesas, estações de trabalho, televisores e notebooks.

Um dos lotes, com aproximadamente 20 cadeiras Cosm Média, da Herman Miller, registrava lance de R$ 100.120 .

Conjunto de 20 cadeiras Herman Miller. — Foto: Reprodução/Kwara

Já uma caixa-bar da marca Artefacto aparecia com lance de R$ 42.600 . Os valores são os registrados na plataforma durante o evento.

Caixa Bar Pietra - Artefacto. — Foto: Reprodução/Kwara

O segundo leilão, intitulado "Desativação de Banco Master e Will Bank (em Liquidação Extrajudicial) – Itens de Cozinha Industrial", tem 258 lotes e encerra dia 30 de novembro, às 13h30.

A lista inclui máquinas de café de grande escala, adegas climatizadas , batedeiras , chopeiras , fornos industriais , televisores , refrigeradores , lava-louças e equipamentos de videoconferência .

Entre os itens anunciados estão uma máquina de café filtrado Bravilor Bonamat, um forno industrial Rational iCombi Pro, uma adega climatizada Art des Caves e um televisor LG de 86 polegadas.

Na página do evento, alguns produtos já aparecem com valores registrados. A máquina de café Bravilor Bonamat, por exemplo, estava anunciada com valor de R$ 35.700 .

Máquina de Café Filtrado de Grande Escala Bravilor Bonamat. — Foto: Reprodução/Kwara

O forno industrial Rational iCombi Pro aparecia por R$ 47.547,50, enquanto o televisor LG de 86 polegadas tinha valor de R$ 4.566,80 .

Forno industrial Rational iCombi Pro. — Foto: Reprodução/Kwara

Os interessados podem consultar a relação completa dos produtos, os valores e as regras de participação diretamente na plataforma Kwara. Para acessar o leilão, clique aqui .

Veja as principais dicas de como não cair em golpes:

Pesquise a reputação do site : consulte o histórico da plataforma em sites de defesa do consumidor, como o Reclame Aqui. Também verifique o portal Leilão Seguro, que mantém uma lista de sites de leilão falsos;

Leia o edital : confira as condições da venda antes de dar um lance. Em leilões de logística reversa e desativação, os produtos são vendidos "no estado em que se encontram" e podem ter avarias, componentes ausentes ou defeitos não aparentes;

Calcule o custo total : o valor do lance não é necessariamente o preço final. Pode haver comissão de 5% do leiloeiro e outras taxas administrativas, dependendo da plataforma;

Confira a retirada : em geral, o produto não é entregue em casa. O arrematante é responsável por desmontar, embalar e transportar o item a partir do local indicado pela organizadora. Verifique no edital os prazos e horários de retirada, além de possíveis multas por atraso ou perda do lote;

Confirme o registro do leiloeiro : verifique se o profissional está registrado na Junta Comercial do estado em que atua. O nome e a matrícula podem ser consultados no site do órgão;

Tenha atenção ao pagamento : em um leilão legítimo, o pagamento deve ser feito para a conta da pessoa jurídica organizadora ou diretamente para a conta do leiloeiro oficial. Evite PIX, TED ou depósitos para contas de terceiros ou CPFs desconhecidos.

Peças de luxo do Banco Master vão a leilão para pagar credores — Foto: Jornal Nacional

articles.title: China estende trégua comercial com os EUA até janeiro de 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão mantém suspensas parte das tarifas e das restrições comerciais entre os dois países; Trump e Xi Jinping devem se reunir na próxima semana, durante cúpula na China.
articles.summary: China estende trégua comercial com os EUA até janeiro de 2027
articles.body:
A China anunciou nesta segunda-feira (9) a prorrogação da trégua comercial com os Estados Unidos por mais dois meses.

O acordo, que estava previsto para terminar nesta terça-feira (10), mantém suspensa parte das tarifas e restrições comerciais impostas pelos dois países durante a guerra comercial entre Estados Unidos e China , marcada por sucessivas retaliações e disputas por tecnologia e influência econômica.

A decisão ocorre às vésperas de um novo encontro entre o presidente americano, Donald Trump, e o líder chinês, Xi Jinping.

➡️ Os dois devem se reunir pela terceira vez neste ano durante a cúpula de líderes da Apec (Fórum de Cooperação Econômica Ásia-Pacífico), que será realizada na China na próxima semana.

Com a prorrogação, a China manterá suspensa por mais dois meses uma tarifa adicional de 24% sobre as importações de produtos americanos. Uma tarifa de 10%, no entanto, continuará em vigor.

A suspensão começa a valer a partir das 13h01 desta terça-feira (10) , segundo comunicado do Conselho de Estado da China, órgão equivalente ao gabinete do governo.

Em setembro, após uma reunião entre Trump e Xi em Washington, os dois países propuseram um pacote de cortes tarifários recíprocos de US$ 60 bilhões (cerca de R$ 330 bilhões).

O plano inclui aproximadamente US$ 17 bilhões (R$ 93,5 bilhões) em produtos agrícolas americanos que foram importados pela China em 2024 como soja, milho, carnes suína e bovina e sorgo. O acordo, porém, ainda não foi finalizado.

Na ocasião, o secretário do Tesouro dos Estados Unidos, Scott Bessent, afirmou que uma nova prorrogação da trégua daria aos dois governos mais tempo para avançar nas negociações econômicas.

China também mantém suspensas restrições a minerais críticos

Xi Jinping e Donald Trump durante encontro na Casa Branca — Foto: Reuters/Evan Vucci

Além das tarifas, Pequim prorrogou até 10 de janeiro de 2027 a suspensão de algumas medidas de controle sobre a exportação de minerais críticos e tecnologias relacionadas.

➡️ As restrições atingem setores considerados estratégicos para a indústria e a tecnologia, já que esses materiais são utilizados na fabricação de produtos e equipamentos de diferentes áreas.

A China também manterá suspensas, até a mesma data, medidas que atingiam 27 empresas americanas. Desse total, 11 fazem parte da lista chinesa de entidades não confiáveis, enquanto outras 16 estão na lista de controle de exportações.

Pequim acusou as 11 empresas de manter cooperação militar e tecnológica com Taiwan, ilha que a China considera parte de seu território. Segundo o governo chinês, essas atividades ameaçavam sua soberania e segurança nacional.

O governo chinês justificou a medida com argumentos de segurança nacional e cumprimento de obrigações internacionais de não proliferação. A restrição proibia exportações de produtos de uso dual, ou seja, itens que podem ter aplicações civis e militares.

Outra medida prorrogada é a suspensão de tarifas portuárias especiais sobre embarcações ligadas aos Estados Unidos.

Investigação sobre setor naval também seguirá suspensa

A China também manterá suspensa uma investigação que apura se a dependência de fornecedores estrangeiros nos setores de transporte marítimo e construção naval representa riscos à segurança do país. A análise envolve, por exemplo, o acesso a navios, equipamentos, tecnologias e serviços necessários para manter essas atividades funcionando.

Pequim ainda decidiu estender por mais dois meses a suspensão das sanções contra cinco unidades da sul-coreana Hanwha Ocean que têm ligações com os Estados Unidos.

Segundo o Ministério do Comércio chinês, a manutenção das suspensões busca colocar em prática os resultados e os entendimentos alcançados na reunião entre Trump e Xi, em Washington.

O governo chinês afirmou ainda que acompanhará os próximos passos dos Estados Unidos e poderá ajustar suas próprias medidas comerciais conforme o andamento das negociações.

articles.summary: Acordo foi fechado com o grupo dinamarquês Carlsberg, que colocou à venda a operação brasileira após uma revisão estratégica; conclusão do negócio é esperada até dezembro deste ano.
articles.body:
Energético Fying Horse e Suco Maguary agora passão a fazer parte do portfólio do Grupo Jav — Foto: Divulgação

O Grupo JAV, conglomerado brasileiro que atua em diferentes setores, da indústria de alimentos à construção civil, assinou um acordo para comprar a Britvic Brasil, dona das marcas Maguary e Flying Horse, informou a agência de notícias Reuters.

A operação foi avaliada em 80 milhões de euros, cerca de R$ 500 milhões na cotação atual.

A venda foi anunciada nesta segunda-feira (9) pelo grupo dinamarquês Carlsberg, atual proprietário da empresa. Segundo a companhia, a decisão ocorreu após uma revisão estratégica que analisou diferentes alternativas para o futuro da operação brasileira.

A Carlsberg tornou-se dona da Britvic Brasil após adquirir, em janeiro de 2025, a operação internacional de refrigerantes da britânica Britvic plc.

A conclusão da operação é esperada até dezembro de 2026. O fechamento do negócio, no entanto, ainda depende das aprovações regulatórias habituais.

Até a conclusão da transação, a Britvic Brasil permanece sob controle da Carlsberg.

articles.title: HSBC upgrades Indian equities to 'overweight', downgrades Chinese stocks to 'neutral'
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's prolonged stock market correction appears to have made its equities more attractive to global investors, with HSBC raising its rating
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's prolonged stock market correction appears to have made its equities more attractive to global investors, with HSBC raising its rating on the market to 'overweight' from 'neutral'. The global financial services firm cited resilient earnings, improving growth prospects and a reset in valuations as reasons behind its more positive stance.In its latest Asia-Pacific equity strategy report, HSBC said India's investment appeal is supported by strong credit growth, improving earnings momentum and policy measures aimed at sustaining economic growth and currency stability.A key factor behind the upgrade is the correction in Indian equity valuations over several years. HSBC said this reset has made valuations more reasonable, particularly among large-cap stocks, after a period in which Indian markets underperformed other emerging markets.There could also be room for more foreign investment in Indian equities. According to the report, just 22 per cent of global emerging market (GEM) funds currently have an overweight position in India, suggesting scope for further allocations.The brokerage also pointed to the resilience of corporate earnings despite challenging macroeconomic conditions."Growth remains resilient despite a series of macro shocks (i.e., higher interest rates and oil)," the report said, adding that the pace of earnings downgrades has become significantly more modest.Another factor supporting India's appeal is its relatively low volatility and the diversification it offers. HSBC said these characteristics are particularly relevant in Asian markets, where artificial intelligence-related stocks are increasingly dominating investment opportunities.Banks, industrials and discretionary consumption among preferred betsHSBC's preferred sectors reflect its positive assessment of India's growth prospects. Banks remain among its favoured segments, with the brokerage pointing to an improved growth outlook.In the industrial space, it identified capital goods, cement, ports and electronic manufacturing services as areas offering opportunities.The brokerage also drew a distinction between consumer discretionary stocks and staples, expressing a preference for the former. Retailers and automobile companies were among its preferred segments within this category.Insurers and hospitals also remained on HSBC's positive list, with the firm highlighting their growth potential despite recent regulatory uncertainties.However, the outlook is not without risks. HSBC flagged elevated crude oil prices and the possibility of an El Niño weather pattern as potential challenges for the Indian economy.The report warned that if energy prices remain high, they could put pressure on domestic demand and the currency. Higher inflation could also weigh on consumption, with rural demand particularly vulnerable.Even so, HSBC does not expect possible earnings downgrades in the coming quarters to be large enough to significantly undermine overall market sentiment.China loses overweight statusWhile HSBC has become more positive on India, its assessment of Chinese equities has turned cautious. The brokerage cut its rating on China to 'neutral' from 'overweight', citing a lack of triggers for a sustained improvement in market valuations.This comes despite attractive valuations and recent policy support. HSBC said weak consumer confidence, persistent difficulties in the property market and softer domestic investment continue to pose challenges to China's growth outlook.Investor activity also points to weaker appetite for Chinese equities. The report highlighted subdued southbound investment flows and declining margin financing, while noting that there are no clear signs of meaningful near-term policy support to strengthen underlying economic growth."Our downgrade reflects our belief that there are limited catalysts that can drive a sustained re-rating," the report said.Despite the downgrade, HSBC continues to see opportunities in select Chinese sectors. Its preferences include banks, consumer stocks offering attractive bond yields, biotechnology and technology hardware companies expected to benefit from the rollout of artificial intelligence.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market and other asset classes given by experts are their own. articles.title: Workplace health costs will take a major bite out of 2027 paychecks
articles.summary: It's open enrollment season for millions of workers making selections in their employer-based health insurance plans for 2027.
articles.body:
It's open enrollment season for millions of workers making selections in their employer-based health insurance plans for 2027.

With healthcare costs a chief concern for Americans already clobbered by inflation, workers will also have to deal with higher monthly premiums, deductibles, and co-pays.

Most employers expect the steepest jump in healthcare costs in more than two decades.

"It's a grim story," Beth Umland, director of employer research for health and benefits at Marsh, told Yahoo Finance. "This is a big cost increase, and there's no getting around that."

What's pushing the higher health insurance costs?

Numerous factors are driving costs higher, including escalating costs for hospital care and prescription drugs, particularly cancer and GLP-1 drugs, as well as a high utilization of patient mental health services, said Matthew Rae, associate director of the Program on the Health Care Marketplace at KFF.

"Worker contributions to family health insurance premiums are only a small portion of the way in which workers pay for their healthcare," Rae added.

Workers pay through cost sharing as well, copays, co-insurances, and deductibles.

"All said, many people with job-based coverage will be chipping in a lot of money to pay for their healthcare next year, either through premiums or through all the costs when they actually use it," he said.

In addition to premiums rising, employees may see a jump in deductibles and other costs.

Workers are paying on average $7,471 annually toward family premiums this year, which is up 9%, or $621, from 2025, according to KFF.

The average deductible is 1,955 for single coverage; family deductibles vary widely by state and are typically over $4,000.

Including the employers' share, total annual premiums for family coverage now average $28,303, up 5% or $1,310 from 2025. Over the same period, wages rose 3.7% and general inflation rose 2.7%, though inflation has been higher in recent months.

"As high trends persist, we expect to see more employers looking for savings in their provider networks, either in terms of changing insurance carriers entirely, limiting choice within the network, or deploying mechanisms to steer members to lower cost options," said Eric Miller , a vice president at Segal, which consults with companies on their benefits.

Take a close look at your plan options. Workers who are reviewing their plan options right now shouldn't be shocked to see higher deductibles and co-pays, said Miller. Some employers are lowering their costs by restricting their employees' choices of doctors or hospitals by adding various tiers to choose from.

articles.title: Micron Will “Buy Back a Hundred Billion Dollars” of Stock at Four Times Earnings
articles.summary: Key TakeawaysOn CNBC’s Halftime Report, a panelist said Micron will buy back $100 billion of stock, about 13% of its roughly $750 billion market value, at ab...
articles.body:
On CNBC's Halftime Report, a panelist said Micron will buy back $100 billion of stock, about 13% of its roughly $750 billion market value, at about 4x next year's earnings.

Buying back that much stock at that price lifts earnings per share by about 15%, and it's still a good deal even if earnings get cut in half.

Micron has authorized $35.16 billion of buybacks starting Dec. 9, and analysts expect $142.9 billion of free cash flow in fiscal 2027.

The main risk is the cycle: Micron last traded near this multiple in 2017 and 2018, just before EPS fell 79%. The first buybacks will show up in the quarter ending in early March.

Micron Technology ( MU:NASDAQ ) is now cheap enough to make investors nervous. Even after a 6% bounce on Friday from a 17% plunge in Thursday's chip rout, the stock trades at 3.9x forward earnings.

On Friday's episode of CNBC's Halftime Report , one panelist argued that the low price is exactly the point:

"If we want to talk about Micron, let's not forget they're going to buy back a hundred billion dollars worth of shares for a market cap that just got a lot cheaper, is 750 billion."

The panelist added that Micron has no debt and plenty of free cash flow, then summed it up: "at literally four times next year's earnings, I'm okay with it." (Strictly speaking, Micron had $5.2 billion of debt at Sept. 3, against $73.45 billion of cash and investments. Close enough.)

A hundred billion dollars is about 13% of the company. At 4x earnings, that's a big deal.

Start with the earnings behind that 4x. Analysts expect Micron's normalized EPS to more than double again in fiscal 2027:

Fiscal 2028 is the estimate I'd watch for cuts. UBS analysts warn that construction pauses after the midterms could threaten around 30% of the US data-center capacity expected to be added that year.

The cash is showing up too. Free cash flow jumped from $1.67 billion in fiscal 2025 to $59.0 billion in fiscal 2026:

Analysts expect $142.9 billion of free cash flow in fiscal 2027 alone, so $100 billion of buybacks would take less than one year's worth. Micron's board hasn't committed to that much yet. It has authorized up to $35.16 billion of repurchases starting Dec. 9, an amount based on a single quarter's free cash flow after dividends. With cash coming in that fast, I'd expect more authorizations to follow.

articles.title: Will probe into Nvidia's Jensen Huang indirectly benefit Indian stock markets?

articles.body: Nvidia, one of the most valuable listed companies in the world, is in the eye of the storm with the company launching an investigation into reports that its chief executive, Jensen Huang, had been the “target of a foreign intelligence effort.” Nvidia shares dropped 8% at the start of trading on Monday.Nvidia's processors are widely used in data centres and computing infrastructure that train and operate AI models. Its most advanced chips have also come under the spotlight because of US export curbs designed to restrict China's access to cutting-edge semiconductor technology.What has happenedNvidia announced the probe on Sunday, following Huang's admission that he had been intimate with a business executive whom US intelligence agencies had reportedly identified as someone collecting information for China, according to The New York Times.The New York Times identified Alice Huang as a former executive at Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based data centre company whose website prominently highlights its partnership with Nvidia.Nvidia ranks among the world's most valuable publicly listed companies, alongside Apple and Microsoft. Its chip sales to China have periodically faced restrictions from US regulators seeking to curb Beijing's access to advanced technology.“The key questions are whether he was aware of any espionage activities and whether any confidential or strategically sensitive information was compromised,” said George Chen, a partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group, a Washington-based consultancy according to AP report.“Those questions require evidence rather than speculation,” he added in a text message to reporters.In recent years, Huang has pressed Washington to ease restrictions on Nvidia's chip exports to China. This year, he secured US President Donald Trump's approval to sell the company's H200 chips to the country. However, it remains uncertain whether Beijing will permit Chinese companies to purchase these processors in substantial volumes.In a regulatory filing in August, Nvidia disclosed that it had sold only a limited quantity of chips to China, citing restrictions imposed by the Chinese government on such purchases.Although the H200 is not among Nvidia's most advanced chip models, it remains a sophisticated processor. Huang had earlier also lobbied Trump for permission to sell the company's less advanced H20 chips, which were specifically designed to comply with US export restrictions on China.China's Foreign Ministry rejected the espionage allegations on Monday, describing them as a smear campaign directed at Beijing.The development has plunged the US chipmaker, a key player in the global artificial intelligence industry, into an unprecedented crisis.The company also lacks a clearly identified successor to its chief executive.The more serious concern is the allegation that Huang “has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.”Nvidia's board has launched an investigation and maintained that it has “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised.”The controversy has surfaced at a particularly difficult moment for the company.Democrats secured control of Congress last week, while candidates advocating closer oversight of artificial intelligence and data-centre construction recorded significant victories.Nvidia was already facing the possibility of tougher congressional scrutiny over whether its advanced chips were reaching China. The latest allegations involving Huang have given lawmakers from both parties further grounds to examine the company.Does it impact India?One would assume that an internal probe in a tech giant in the US would have no impact whatsoever on Indian stock markets.But, Sensex and Nifty which have delivered negative returns in the last year may actually benefit indirectly from this development. Globally stock markets have rallied on the artificial intelligence and chip-led boom with Nvidia actually leading the rally.India on the other hand has missed out on the AI stock boom, one of the major factors cited for exit of foreign investors from the stock market.But after months of underperformance, Indian equities have recently regained investor interest as concerns grow over concentrated investments in AI. Investors are increasingly looking towards factors such as lower crude oil prices and robust domestic corporate earnings. Last week, India emerged as one of Asia's most prominent beneficiaries of the so-called anti-AI trade.The positive sentiment towards Indian equities received another boost on Monday, with two more banks turning bullish on the market. HSBC upgraded Indian stocks to overweight from neutral, while Citigroup increased its 12-month target for the Nifty 50.Nvidia is at the heart of the AI investment boom and has increasingly relied on its own balance sheet and credit strength to support faster infrastructure spending.Bloomberg Opinion columnist Shuli Ren has described Huang as the “central banker of AI.” The question she raises is particularly relevant now: Will Nvidia's money keep flowing now that the central banker himself is in trouble?According to a Bloomberg analysis, while Huang's troubles alone are not a sufficient basis for an investment case for India, but if the controversy deepens doubts about the AI trade and prompts investors to diversify beyond it, Indian equities could benefit from an unusual advantage that the country does not have a giant, expensive AI sector.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. articles.title: Analysts say Nvidia CEO unlikely to be ousted over affair, but raise questions about company's future
articles.summary: Analysts on Wall Street say the Nvidia CEO's job is likely safe, but that his affair could increase scrutiny of the company.
articles.body:
Wall Street analysts are reacting to news of Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy with a mixture of caution and concern about the company's future and what the episode means for the AI industry.

Nvidia stock fell in early trading Monday.

In an email to Nvidia employees , Jensen Huang admitted to the affair and apologized to his family. The company's board has launched an independent investigation into the matter, but noted that it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised."

The woman, Alice Huang, was an executive at Singapore data center company MegaSpeed, which has been the subject of investigations into whether it smuggled Nvidia chips into China.

One of the company's co-founders, Jensen Huang, is instrumental to the AI boom and closely guides Nvidia's strategy.

Moor Insights & Strategy CEO and chief analyst Patrick Moorhead told Yahoo Finance that he doesn't believe Huang will be pushed out unless the board's investigation turns up anything.

"The issue is that Jensen is the product strategist, the closer with the hyperscalers, and the face of the company in Washington and Beijing. This story puts that last role at risk," Moorehead said.

Wedbush analyst Matt Bryson wrote in a note to investors that the board's initial statement reduces the chances that it plans to oust Huang, but said doing so would be a significant negative for the company due to his "hands-on operating style."

But he wrote that the incident could hurt the CEO's credibility.

"Regardless of the outcome of the investigation, however, we necessarily see Jensen losing some of his power/credibility in advocating for AI and Nvidia with US government representatives (whether free trade with foreign entities or how the government regulates AI development)," Bryson wrote.

Mizuho analyst Jordan Klein, meanwhile, wrote in a note following the news that the board investigation will likely overshadow Nvidia's earnings report on Nov. 17.

"A lot of risk associated with Jensen Huang and his status as CEO…cannot be hedged out. He is too important for NVDA and the entire industry. I would assume the investigation finds no serious wrongdoing or anything criminal. Jensen likely remains CEO; nothing changes in the long run," Klein said.

Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon pointed out that the incident will increase scrutiny of Nvidia in Washington.

The headlines are "(at the very best) going to be a heavy distraction, and at the worst provide significant ammunition to both sides of the aisle, from China hawks (of which there are many on Capitol Hill) already displeased with the current US stance toward the country, to incoming Democrats unhappy with the close ties to Trump that Jensen has cultivated over the last few years," he wrote in an investor note.

articles.title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long
articles.summary: Kashim Chowdhury has been convicted of fraud after pocketing £284,000 of taxpayers' money over three years.
articles.body:
Aleesha Adams joined a video call with Kashim Chowdhury in May 2023.

He'd been on sick leave from his job at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) for nearly three months and Adams, his line manager, wanted to put a plan in action to ease him back into work.

At the start of the call, Chowdhury was coughing and waving tissues up to the camera in an attempt to show how ill he was. But what really caught Adams' attention was how pale he looked.

She noticed white powder had started separating from his forehead. "He was sweating, it was like rubbing off, so it was darker underneath and darker on the neck," she told his trial.

She claimed he was wearing white make-up to look sick. Something he denied in court.

Little did she know UKHSA was not Chowdhury's only employer.

That month, he was also being paid to work full-time for the Department for the Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office. He was contracted to work 183 hours a week – more than the number of hours in seven days. He fraudulently earned more than £284,000 of taxpayers' money.

In total, he had eight overlapping full-time public-sector jobs between 2020 and 2023. During that time, this relatively junior civil servant was paid £350,000.

Soon after her call with Chowdhury, Adams discovered that he had logged into the call using a Defra email address. When she challenged him about it, he blamed it on a technical error. She told the jury at his trial at Southwark Crown Court: "I believed he was lying." She escalated her concerns up the chain.

But his fraudulent behaviour remained undetected. Chowdhury was able to keep working multiple government jobs until September 2023 when he left the Civil Service.

He was finally caught in 2024 by the government's National Fraud Initiative, which conducts searches of Civil Service databases, such as payroll, every two years to look for anomalies.

On Monday he was found guilty of nine counts of fraud and told by the judge that he would be facing a "very substantial custodial sentence".

Chowdhury, 56, arrived each day at court alone. He is married, yet there never seemed to be any friends or family there to support him.

He would often make his way down the corridors of the court building carrying two plastic carrier bags, with a bobble hat perched on his head.

He sometimes looked bewildered in the witness box.

Chowdhury, who had a diagnosis of PTSD in 2015, said that he had taken on so many roles because he feared losing his livelihood after experiencing insecure employment. He said he'd been forced out of a job at the Department for Education in 2013.

He said he hadn't been thinking clearly when applying for jobs ''because of my stress, distress and trauma and due to my panic at the time".

But the prosecution argued his behaviour was "deliberate" and "intentional dishonesty" and that he had exploited the system.

However, the case raises important questions for the Civil Service. How was he able to get away with it for so long?

Part of the explanation is that the Civil Service's human resources system is not centralised. Chowdhury did not declare on government application forms that he was already a civil servant, so the system did not spot the duplication.

Hannah Keenan, who works at the Institute for Government, says the system clearly failed. "Government departments are taking hiring decisions independently of each other and without systems that join up," she said.

"That the model and the culture surrounding it aren't working shouldn't be a surprise though - we've known for a long time about poor performers flying under the radar by shuffling between jobs."

There are more than 550,000 people employed across the Civil Service, many in offices in Whitehall, in central London. They are responsible for carrying out government policy and the daily administration of the country.

Another reason why Chowdhury's fraud went undetected is that he was working entirely from the east London house he shared with his mother. In 2023, she had dementia and terminal cancer, and he told his employers that he needed to be at home to look after her.

But rather than reducing his workload to concentrate on her care, he took on more jobs. He covered up his impossible daily schedule by getting sick notes from his GP.

In April 2023, he was off with what he called "mixed anxiety and depressive disorder" from Defra, the UKHSA, the Department for Business and Trade and the Food Standards Agency.

While the sick notes were shown to the jury, they were not given evidence about what caused the depressive disorder or of a psychiatric assessment having been done during this period.

His sickness did not prevent him from starting yet another job – this time at the Home Office. He did not mention to them he was ill, nor did he tell them he was working elsewhere.

Unsurprisingly, a succession of his line managers told the jury he had not been very good at his jobs.

Especially damning was the evidence given by Dan McCartney, who managed Chowdhury at Defra. He said he had to "effectively tell him what to do the whole time" and that Chowdhury kept his camera off during video calls for four months, claiming technical problems.

But because Chowdhury was not subject to any formal performance measures at Defra, he was given a permanent job. He remained there for two years.

In September 2023, Chowdhury was found to have more than £40,000 in his bank accounts as well as significant investments, including £45,000 in premium bonds.

A recent survey of 1,700 civil servants by the independent think tank Re:State found 76% of respondents thought it did not do a good job of tackling poor performers.

An ex-senior civil servant told the BBC that much of the Civil Service is culturally averse to performance management.

"Whitehall's known for ages it has to be less risk averse. Shrinking the Civil Service and the adoption of artificial intelligence technology make that more vital," they said.

"But don't underestimate the fear factor: fear of drawn-out grievances and fear of being accused of wasting taxpayers' money if the Civil Service was to do what big private sector firms do, which is cut to get rid of poor performers by offering some money and a settlement agreement."

A Defra spokesperson said: "Kashim Chowdhury abused the trust placed in him as a public servant and defrauded taxpayers out of almost £285,000. He will now rightly face the consequences for his actions.

"This conviction is the result of a thorough and painstaking investigation led by the Defra Counter Fraud and Investigations team. It sends a clear message that fraud against the public purse will not be tolerated and those responsible will be held to account."

The spokesperson said Defra would use "all available avenues to recover the proceeds of Chowdhury's offending on behalf of taxpayers".

Chowdhury's case also illustrates a wider issue.

He was engaged in what is being called "polygamous working", where people hold down several jobs secretly. Websites have even been set up offering people advice on how to keep their employers in the dark.

Its rise has been blamed on larger numbers of people working from home.

The government's National Fraud Initiative has identified 23 cases of "polygamous working" across London in its most recent report. It uncovered £500,000 of overpaid salaries over a period of a few months.

Alongside the fraud case, Chowdhury is involved in a legal dispute with his three siblings, who accuse him of ''bullying'' their mother into signing over half of her £2.1m home to him in the final days of her life. He denies it.

At times during his criminal trial, Chowdhury appeared confused by what he was hearing and blamed trauma for the web of lies he had spun. The jury took seven hours to reach their verdict and decided he was motivated by personal gain - stealing tens of thousands of pounds from the taxpayer.

Chowdhury now faces a significant custodial sentence.

Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud

articles.title: Nvidia has a 'deep bench' if Jensen Huang steps aside, tech investor says
articles.summary: What does life after Jensen Huang even look like?
articles.body:
Nvidia can still crush it in the coming years if embattled CEO Jensen Huang is forced to step away from the company.

When asked how important Huang is to the next few years of the AI chip darling, Niles Investment Management founder and longtime tech investor Dan Niles told Sozzi Unleashed that he "isn't."

"[Huang's] got a very deep bench, and a historical example is what happened to Apple after Steve Jobs passed away. … Did it collapse?" Niles said. "So Jensen's done a great job of empowering people underneath him. I think one thing that will happen is there will be a successor appointed. The board will force that. And so I think that will occur out of this."

"Are the products in the pipeline, much like when Steve Jobs passed away, that will keep the company going for the next couple of years? Absolutely," Niles added. "But is Jensen very important to the company? Completely. So those are two separate thoughts. But they can both coexist."

Nvidia's board of directors has launched an independent investigation into reports that a woman CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with was allegedly spying on him for the Chinese government.

Huang admitted to the affair on Sunday in an email to employees.

Nvidia stock fell 5% on Monday as a dark cloud settled over Nvidia and its once-Teflon CEO's future.

Niles said this is a "horrible" situation for Huang, someone he has known for 30 years.

"The big question every Nvidia and tech investor is asking this morning … Will Jensen stay on as CEO of Nvidia?" Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives wrote in a note. "The Board investigation will be key and investors are factoring in Jensen will stay on as CEO with a small chance he ultimately is removed or steps aside and the stock is down modestly accordingly. Jensen is the core DNA of Nvidia and its AI success and ambitions are heavily tied to him staying on as CEO."

Ives added, "Jensen is not replaceable ... there is no other person on the management team bench that can step in seamlessly as CEO and that speaks to the key risk now with Nvidia that investors will factor this dynamic to the stock. Jensen has become the global face of the AI Revolution and that now will be front and center for Nvidia how to navigate this very difficult situation looking forward."

articles.title: October inflation data is expected to be cooler, helped by steadying energy prices
articles.summary: Economists expect a 0.3% month-over-month jump in prices in October, reflecting cooler but still-sticky inflation.
articles.body:
October inflation data coming on Tuesday is expected to show that inflation cooled somewhat from September's elevated levels but remains sticky.

Economists surveyed by Bloomberg expect the Consumer Price Index to rise 0.3% in October compared to a month earlier, a far slower pace than September's 0.6% gain. Core inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, is seen rising 0.2%, down from 0.3% a month earlier.

October's report is unlikely to include annual inflation figures because the Bureau of Labor Statistics was unable to publish full October 2025 data due to the government shutdown last year. But some economists estimate that inflation accelerated slightly on a year-over-year basis.

Rising energy prices weighed heavily on September's report , but October's price increases look less dramatic.

"We expect more subdued CPI in October after two straight disappointing 0.3% gains in the core rate," Dave Sloan, senior economist for North America at Continuum Economics, wrote in a note. "Gasoline prices have seen only a marginal rise on the month, and we expect overall CPI to also rise by 0.2%."

Inflation on many goods likely eased last month as tariff pressures faded, though goods inflation has been running hot in recent months due to intense artificial intelligence demand and rising vehicle prices, Bank of America economist Stephen Juneau wrote in a note. Services inflation is likely sticky due to factors like rising airfare prices, he added.

"Although we expect monthly core CPI to moderate, we see the risks as skewed to the upside," the note said. "The two biggest sources of uncertainty are used cars and health insurance."

Tuesday's inflation data is the Federal Reserve's final look at the CPI before it meets Dec. 8-9, although it will get another look at inflation data via its preferred measure, the Personal Consumption Expenditures index, later this month.

With the labor market holding up , and even showing signs of accelerating, traders currently see an 83% chance that the central bank raises benchmark interest rates by 25 basis points. Another sticky inflation report is likely to cement those odds.

Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

articles.title: Thanksgiving gas is on track for a record, even after a 6-week slide
articles.summary: Pump prices just fell for a sixth straight week, while diesel, the fuel that moves nearly everything else, has barely budged from its record.
articles.body:
Gas prices just fell for a sixth straight week. Thanksgiving drivers are still on track to pay more than ever.

Regular gas averaged $4.01 a gallon on Monday, according to AAA . That's down about 10% from its latest peak of nearly $4.48 in late September, based on US Energy Information Administration data.

Wholesale prices have fallen about twice as fast. Gasoline futures ( RB=F ) slid about 21% from Sept. 18 through Friday's close, as oil ( CL=F ) dropped about 20% from its April high.

Pump prices have typically run about $1 per gallon above futures prices. Based on Friday's close, that points to roughly $3.70 to $3.80 a gallon, or another 20 to 30 cents of relief, by Yahoo Finance calculations.

"That'll be a 3-handle by mid-next week," market analyst Mike Zaccardi posted on X on Nov. 6, when the average stood at $4.07.

Even that would leave holiday drivers paying a record. The highest Thanksgiving-week average in EIA data going back to 1990 is $3.65, set in 2022. The latest weekly reading, for the week of Nov. 2, was $4.15.

Adjusted for inflation, though, this year's $4.50 peak in May comes to about $4.53 in current dollars, far below 2022's $5.71 and 2008's $6.33, by Yahoo Finance calculations.

The slide picked up speed in the week of the Nov. 3 midterms , when pump prices fell 12 cents, the most since June. ING economist James Smith doesn't expect the election to change much.

"Sure, gasoline prices mattered enormously to US voters, and politicians have been surprisingly frank about that," Smith wrote in a Nov. 6 note. "But if diplomacy could not deliver a solution before the elections, why should it suddenly do so now the political clock has reset for two years?"

The fuel that moves goods by truck and rail hit a record $6.53 a gallon in the week of Sept. 21 and was still about $6.17 on Nov. 9, according to AAA . US stockpiles fell below 100 million barrels in late October, the lowest since 2003, the EIA said .

Those costs are showing up across corporate America. S&P 500 companies mentioned "inflation" or "inflationary" 820 times on October earnings calls, the most since February 2024, Bloomberg reported , as fuel, fertilizer and plastic resin got pricier.

The open question, Chris Versace of TheStreet Pro wrote Monday, is "the length of time to bring supply levels back to normal. That will help dictate how quickly inflation pressures fade, and with it margin relief for companies."

The EIA's next weekly reading is due Monday evening; October Consumer Price Index data follows Tuesday, and the Thanksgiving-week reading comes Nov. 23.

articles.title: Fed officials on watch for overheating demand as they weigh interest rate path
articles.summary: Federal Reserve officials are monitoring the strength of demand in the US economy as they consider how high interest rates need to go to tame inflation.
articles.body:
Federal Reserve officials are monitoring the strength of demand in the US economy as they consider how high interest rates need to go to tame inflation.

Despite expected moratoriums on data centers in several states, Chicago Fed president Austan Goolsbee said Monday that the AI build-out is starting to look like more than just "old-fashioned demand overheating," noting that, anecdotally, everyone is trying to hire an electrician at the same time, which could cause prices to go up.

"The danger with that is nobody ever was under the impression that [inflation] just goes away on its own," Goolsbee said during a Q&A at the Chicago Fed. "If you get the economy overheated, the conventional wisdom is be aggressive up front to never let the economy overheat because once it gets overheated, it's extremely painful to get rid of that kind of overheating. So I think we got to watch out in that space."

Richmond Fed president Tom Barkin was a little more cautious, saying Monday that while inflation remains stubborn, there are risks to the durability of demand in the economy and that the Fed needs to move cautiously as it raises rates to tame inflation, so as not to knock the economy off course.

"With demand healthy and inflation stubbornly elevated, the appropriate direction of monetary policy is relatively straightforward," Barkin said in a speech in South Carolina. "However, risks to the demand outlook remain easy to envision. Because of that, it is wise to move policy with care."

Barkin noted that strong corporate earnings have been driven by explosive growth in the tech sector and strong demand, which has boosted profits for companies that had planned conservatively. Not to mention that GDP grew at 3.4% in the third quarter and productivity grew at 3.6% while wages have remained subdued.

However, Barkin said he wonders how long this earnings strength can last, noting that he's hearing widespread reports of broad-based cost pressures across health insurance, gas and diesel prices, trucking and ocean freight, memory chips, interest rates, and tariffs.

"The question is how businesses will react to margin pressure as we move into next year," Barkin said. "Will they find new avenues for growth? Scale back headcount and investment? Or find a way to recover these costs by raising their prices further?"

Barkin added that there's a question about the durability of consumer strength as well, noting that even as real incomes have flattened, consumers have found ways to keep spending. He said consumers are trading down to private labels and discount retailers, moving from beef to cheaper proteins, or turning to local food banks to supplement groceries. They're also making trade-offs by buying used items instead of new ones and choosing to repair rather than replace.

articles.title: Vanguard and Fidelity have a warning for retirement savers
articles.summary: Experts say that lower expected returns could signal to savers that it's time to take a closer look at their retirement plans.
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

Fidelity and Vanguard recently released long-term forecasts for stock market returns, and both companies delivered a sobering outlook for retirees: Long-term investment returns are either modest or expected to decline.

Vanguard's 10-year outlook suggests that U.S. stocks will deliver an average annual return between 4.8% and 6.8% over the next decade. Fidelity's 20-year forecast projects an annualized return of 5.8% for U.S. stocks, or about 3.2% after inflation. That compares with the S&P 500's historical average of roughly 10% since it launched in 1957.

For retirees, these projections could translate to slower growth over time and less money in their retirement accounts if these predictions hold or decrease.

What lower stock returns could mean for your retirement savings

If you don't follow the stock market but do invest in stocks or stock funds through a 401(k) or IRA, these projections shouldn't be ignored.

These forecasts suggest that your retirement savings may grow more slowly over the next decade or two, and while this could change over time, it may be a good time to revisit your long-term retirement strategy.

"While the stock market's trajectory is relatively unpredictable, it is possible that if its returns fall below historical averages, savers could be surprised by the pace of their retirement cushion's growth," said Brianna Rodgers, director of investor education at Madison Trust Company. "Those with certain expectations surrounding consistent market growth may see an impact in their savings when compounded over a set number of years."

Ultimately, most experts would agree that the stock market is unpredictable and could be affected by a range of future economic and geopolitical events that are impossible to foresee.

This doesn't mean you shouldn't take projections into consideration; it just means that instead of building a retirement plan that assumes the best-case scenario and maximum growth potential, you might want to consider building a savings plan that gets you to your desired savings target and funds your retirement lifestyle in your ideal timeline even if there are a few downturns along the way.

3 moves savers can make to account for potentially lower returns

Start by reviewing where your savings stand now and how they're projected to grow, then adjust as needed. Whether you plan to retire in a few years or have decades to go, these steps can help keep you on track.

Reevaluate your timeline and savings needs

Slower growth could mean that you could end up with less money for retirement than anticipated or that you may need to work longer to continue saving and give that money more time to compound.

"Those who are approaching retirement may consider postponing their retirement altogether if returns are markedly lower than anticipated. This can also translate to a complete overhaul regarding investment and withdrawal strategies, as well as overall lifestyle practices," Rodgers said. "Nevertheless, while market projections have the potential to be correct, their outcomes can never be guaranteed."

You may also be overestimating your retirement costs . While some expenses, such as healthcare and travel, tend to creep up in later years, others, such as housing, childcare, and even debt payments, can decrease with age. You'll also want to make sure you're not overlooking other forms of income, such as Social Security benefits that could change how aggressively you need to be saving for retirement.

Make a plan to boost your retirement contributions

Saving early and consistently is key. Review your budget and current contribution rate to determine if there's room to increase those contributions. Even if you can't do so immediately, some retirement plans offer automatic increase plans that gradually increase your contribution over time, typically after performance reviews or raises. That way you don't have to adjust your rate manually, and your contribution rate increases as your income increases.

If your employer matches contributions, make sure you're contributing enough to get the full match. It's one of the easiest ways to grow your savings.

Review diversification and asset allocation regularly

Putting your retirement savings on autopay may seem like enough, but neglecting your strategy can be costly.

Your portfolio allocation, or the mix of different types of investments in your portfolio, can impact your returns over time and how much risk you're exposed to. Make it a habit to review your retirement portfolio allocation regularly as your timeline, goals, and risk tolerance change.

"Observing market forecasts can prove to be beneficial, but it's often not encouraged to base one's retirement strategies entirely off predictions," Rodgers said. "Rather, investors can take this moment to gauge their current saving habits and existing strategies. Consider evaluating whether your portfolio is appropriately diversified and whether any of your present investments put you in a position outside of your risk tolerance."

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a reported Chinese spy damages this key investing factor
articles.summary: It will take a while for Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to earn back trust.
articles.body:
Investing in a public company's stock is more than crunching numbers.

I have heard from a lot of you about the hot water that Nvidia's ( NVDA ) celebrated CEO, Jensen Huang, is in following his admission to having cheated on his wife of 40-plus years with a reported Chinese spy. I said on X (see below) that Nvidia is now in its first true crisis, arguably since its founding in 1993.

Some of you pushed back on me for coining it a crisis, calling attention to Nvidia's strong demand pipeline and leadership position in AI chips. I suspect Jensen's vision has helped make you a lot of money through the years, so I get why the first instinct is to sweep this under the rug and voice support for Huang.

I am not going to deny that you have a point on the fundamentals of the business. I also won't deny that Huang is a generational founder of a transformational business.

But make no mistake: This is a crisis created by Huang that didn't need to happen. And it all boils down to trust .

If Huang can have an affair with a reported Chinese spy, can we trust what he says about AI demand being off the charts for as far as the eye can see? Can we trust that he didn't divulge company secrets to this person? Can we trust that this is a one-off for him and that he will emerge as a changed human being? Can we trust that he will finally put forth a clear succession plan?

Then there is this other aspect of trust.

Nvidia is not only one of the world's most valuable companies, with a market cap of $4.5 trillion, but it has also lent its own creditworthiness to drive AI infrastructure growth in the US and around the world. Over the past three years, the chip giant has reportedly offered $300 billion in financial support to customers, in addition to investing billions into risky AI startups, including neoclouds like CoreWeave ( CRWV ).

At the epicenter of this is trust in Jensen Huang, the human, and trust in Jensen Huang leading the company at such a level that he can make good on all these financial commitments. And as he makes good on these financial commitments, his wallet will stay open to support the AI ecosystem in good times and bad.

We can agree to disagree on this being an Nvidia crisis. But there is no disagreement on Jensen Huang having breached the trust of his investors, big and small.

articles.body: MUMBAI: The total shareholding of private promoters in NSE-listed companies has been moving northwards for the last two quarters, and at nearly 42%, it is now at a three-year high. The rise in aggregate holding by these promoters came after a secular fall in their holding from Dec 2021 till March 2026, an analysis by an arm of Prime Database showed. articles.title: In Noel's crosshairs, Chandra, Mehli reconnect at Tata HQ
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Fresh from Italy, where Tata Motors announced the acquisition of commercial vehicle maker Iveco, Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran invited Mehli
articles.body: MUMBAI: Fresh from Italy, where Tata Motors announced the acquisition of commercial vehicle maker Iveco, Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran invited Mehli Mistry, the late Ratan Tata's confidant and a trustee of the Tata Education and Development Trust, to Bombay House on Thursday.Coming just days after the two were seen together at the wedding celebrations of Mehli's daughter Laila, the meeting reinforced a belief within Tata circles that relations between the two are improving after more than a year marked by a broader power shift within the Tata Group following the death of Ratan Tata.People familiar with the matter said Chandrasekaran and Mehli, who was voted out of the two principal trusts that hold majority in Tata Sons by Noel Tata and others, discussed issues that had affected their ties. Mehli's challenge against his removal is pending before the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner.Mehli and Chandrasekaran's conversation last week was focused on rebuilding trust and restoring a working equation. Mehli later left for Dubai, with both sides appearing keen to move beyond a difficult period in one of Tata Group's most significant internal relationships.For much of the past decade, Mehli and Chandrasekaran were regarded as allies. After the dramatic ouster of Cyrus Mistry as chairman of Tata Sons in 2016, Mehli played a key role in the legal fight that followed between Cyrus and Ratan Tata. When Ratan Tata had to choose a successor, he picked Chandrasekaran, assisted by Mehli. Mehli later backed Chandrasekaran's second and third terms as chairman of Tata Sons. The third term, however, became contentious after Noel Tata, who succeeded Ratan Tata as chairman of Tata Trusts, opposed Chandrasekaran's reappointment.Mehli and Chandrasekaran's relationship survived differences in personality and style. Those who know Mehli describe him as intensely loyal, fiercely independent and refreshingly blunt. Friends admire his willingness to say in a room what others prefer to whisper outside it. Critics point to a temperament that can run ahead of diplomacy. The redeeming feature, according to people who have worked closely with him, is that his anger rarely lingers.Chandrasekaran is a different kind of leader. Publicly measured and understated, he has cultivated the image of a consensus-builder since arriving at Bombay House. Yet colleagues say beneath that calm exterior lies a highly competitive executive with sharp political instincts and an acute understanding of institutional power.Then came the post-Ratan Tata era. Ratan Tata's death in Oct 2024 altered the balance of influence within Tata Trusts, the largest shareholder of Tata Sons. Disagreements that had previously been settled privately soon surfaced within the trusts. Mehli and fellow Tata Trusts trustees Darius Khambata, Pramit Jhaveri and Jehangir Jehangir argued that information on Tata Sons covered under Article 121 of the company's Articles of Association had not been shared with them, limiting their ability to take informed decisions. The four trustees voted Vijay Singh off the Tata Sons board.Concerns about the emerging situation prompted a visit to Delhi by Noel, Tata Trusts vice-chairman Venu Srinivasan, Khambata and Chandrasekaran, who briefed senior government officials on governance issues within the trusts.Mehli, who was inducted into Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) by Ratan Tata and remained one of his most trusted advisers, increasingly found himself at odds with the emerging power structure. He was eventually voted out of the two trusts by Noel, Srinivasan and Singh, who is also a vice-chairman of the trusts.The impasse followed restrictions imposed by the MCC on SRTT, preventing it from joining SDTT in nominating a joint representative for quorum purposes.You use AI every day. articles.title: US, China drink less, India begins pouring more
articles.summary: BENGALURU: The world's two biggest alcohol markets are drinking less, but India seems to be in the mood for another round.
articles.body: BENGALURU: The world's two biggest alcohol markets are drinking less, but India seems to be in the mood for another round. Alcohol consumption volumes in the country jumped 10% in the first half of 2026, the fastest growth among 21 major markets tracked by drinks research firm IWSR, according to estimates shared exclusively with TOI.India was also the only country among these markets where consumption increased across every category and subcategory tracked by IWSR. From beer and whisky to vodka, gin and wine, Indians consumed more of almost everything, even as the wider global drinks industry struggled with falling demand.Beer led the growth, with full-strength beer consumption rising 16% year-on-year during Jan-June. Ready-to-drink (RTD) alcoholic beverages, which include premixed cocktails and other packaged drinks, grew 12%, while Indian whisky, one of the country's largest spirits categories, recorded 4% growth.Blended Scotch whisky volumes rose 8%, while vodka and gin grew 6% each. Rum and non-Cognac brandy recorded 3% growth apiece. Still wine consumption increased 2%, while fortified wine grew 7%. Interestingly, the fastest growth among the major subcategories for which IWSR shared India-specific figures came from beer without the booze. No-alcohol beer consumption surged 25%, outpacing every major alcoholic drink category in percentage terms. The numbers stand in sharp contrast to trends elsewhere. Across the 21 markets covered by IWSR, which account for 76% of global beverage alcohol consumption, total volumes fell 1% in the first half of 2026.The US, the world's largest alcohol market alongside China, recorded a 4% decline in consumption, while China saw volumes fall 3%. Beer consumption declined 4% in the US and 2% in China, compared with India's 16% growth.Remove the US and China from the calculations, however, and alcohol consumption across the remaining markets actually grew 1%.India topped the growth charts, followed by Colombia at 9%, South Africa at 5%, Brazil at 3% and the UK at 2%. Mexico and Thailand also reported growth, although IWSR did not specify the rates."India continues to be one of the most important markets for the beverage alcohol industry worldwide. This latest data just reinforces this narrative. Global brands that want to expand internationally are increasingly looking to India as a key source of their growth plans," said Marten Lodewijks, president and managing director of IWSR, told TOI. The contrast is visible across individual drinks too. While still wine consumption declined 4% across the 21 markets, it grew 2% in India. No-alcohol beer volumes increased 8% across these markets, compared with India's 25% rise.IWSR said growing moderation trends and the use of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs were putting pressure on alcohol consumption globally. Inflation, tariffs and economic uncertainty have also weighed on US consumers, while China's slowing economy and other structural challenges have affected demand.You use AI every day.
