articles.title: Uber Engineering Leader for Robotaxis, Delivery Network to Exit
articles.summary: A longtime Uber Technologies Inc. executive leading engineering efforts for robotaxi partnerships and core services for maps and memberships is leaving, addi...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- A longtime Uber Technologies Inc. executive leading engineering efforts for robotaxi partnerships and core services for maps and memberships is leaving, adding to a string of recent executive departures at the ride-hailing giant.

Danny Guo, who reports to Chief Technology Officer Praveen Neppalli Naga as the vice president of engineering and science, will step down next Monday, according to an email sent to employees on Monday. He will be taking a role outside the transportation industry, an Uber spokesperson said in response to a Bloomberg News inquiry. Guo did not respond to a request for comment.

Guo, who has been with Uber for nearly 12 years, oversees engineering and science functions across several key businesses, including autonomous initiatives, the Uber One subscription program and the back-end network for deliveries, according to his Linkedin profile. Many of the leaders under each of those teams will now report to Naga, the spokesperson said.

Guo is the latest company veteran to depart in recent months for opportunities elsewhere. Last week, OpenAI announced that it hired Jill Hazelbaker, Uber's president and longtime communications executive, as its corporate affairs chief.

Some of the high-profile departures have been at the company's autonomous-vehicle division: Sarfraz Maredia, Uber's global head of autonomous mobility and delivery, is also set to leave next week, Bloomberg reported last month. The unit's head of business development for autonomous partnerships and head of legal also left in recent months.

The company has seen major organizational upheaval after it announced plans to cut 10% of the entire workforce in September, aimed at reducing bureaucracy.

Uber last week reported third-quarter earnings that met expectations, with ride-hailing and delivery bookings sustaining 20% growth for a fifth quarter row. But investors have expressed concerns as autonomous vehicles have become commonplace, which they worry might threaten Uber's pioneering business. The company's stock has fallen 13% this year through Monday's close.

The company has said it will commit more than $10 billion to its robotaxi partnerships with other technology developers over the coming years, rather than building its own autonomous vehicle. But it has ways to go to catch up with Alphabet Inc.'s Waymo, which it regards as both a partner and a competitor. Uber said it hopes to have more than 2,000 driverless taxis available for customers in 2027, trailing the 4,000 vehicles that Waymo has across the US today.

articles.title: Fed’s Goolsbee says data center buildout ‘overheating’ economy
articles.summary: Austan Goolsbee, the president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, said Monday that the data center buildout is “overheating” the economy and putting upward pressure on prices. “Now this stuff with the AI data center buildout is, to my eye, starting to look more just like old-fashioned demand overheating,” Goolsbee told Subrina Hudson of…
articles.body:
Austan Goolsbee, the president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, said Monday that the data center buildout is “overheating” the economy and putting upward pressure on prices.

“Now this stuff with the AI data center buildout is, to my eye, starting to look more just like old-fashioned demand overheating,” Goolsbee told Subrina Hudson of the Chicago Sun-Times at a Leadership Greater Chicago event.

Goolsbee added the “danger” of the economy overheating is that “nobody ever was under the impression that that just goes away on its own,” saying central bankers must be “aggressive up front” to prevent it from occurring in the first place.

More than 1,500 data centers were in development nationwide as of August, the Pew Research Center reported , citing Data Center Map .

Fed officials have referenced the rapid artificial intelligence buildout as a contributing to persistent inflation, along with energy price shocks from the Iran war and President Trump’s tariffs .

“I see some economy-wide pressure from AI-fueled demand,” Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook said in September . “Data-center investment relies on inputs, like construction labor and energy, that are broadly used in many sectors in the economy.

“As a result, increased AI investment could introduce price pressure to those other sectors.”

Inflation in September was 3.7 percent , according to the consumer price index (CPI). The Bureau of Labor Statistics will release CPI data for October on Tuesday.

Stubborn inflation led Fed officials to raise interest rates by a quarter point in September, the first hike in more than three years.

After officials held rates steady last month, traders are pricing in an 84.2 percent chance of another quarter-point increase at the Fed’s next meeting in early December, according to the CME FedWatch tool .

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh has also touched on AI’s impact on the economy, saying in September that central bank officials “care much about the implications” of the technology “on the demand side.”

Shortly after he took over at the Fed in May, Warsh formed a task force dedicated to assess the economic impact of AI.

Warsh has said he expects the task force , which Andreessen Horowitz co-founder March Andreessen and Stanford University economist Charles Jones are overseeing, to deliver its initial report by the end of this year.

articles.body:
President Trump on Monday announced a special envoy for manufacturing in a post to Truth Social.

“I am proud to announce that David MacNeil, the GREAT American entrepreneur and founder of WeatherTech, will be the Special Envoy for Manufacturing!” Trump said in his Monday afternoon post.

“David has built an incredible American company that makes outstanding products, RIGHT HERE IN THE U.S.A. He knows how to create jobs, bring Manufacturing back home, and put America First,” the president added.

MacNeil owns the WeatherTech brand , which sells car and home accessories like floor mats and phone holders. He founded the company in 1989.

“Together, we will bring back American jobs, strengthen our factories, and make sure that future products are MADE IN AMERICA. Congratulations David — Your unparalleled expertise is vitally needed!” Trump wrote in the Monday post.

Trump’s Monday envoy announcement follows a blowout midterm election last week in which his party struggled amid Americans’ concerns about the cost of living. Democrats took direct aim at the president’s trade policy during campaign season, and now appear posed to challenge him on it as they retake congressional power.

articles.title: Skydance plans to bundle HBO Max and Paramount+ next year
articles.summary: It’s part of an industrywide trend toward bundling — and a prelude to further integration between the two streaming services.
articles.body: Skydance will start selling HBO Max and Paramount+ together in a streaming bundle early next year, the company said Monday. It’s part of an industrywide trend toward bundling — and a prelude to further integration between the two streaming services. “Long-term, the plan is basically to bring them together,” Skydance CEO David Ellison said last month when the media mega-merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery took effect. Skydance is the parent company of CNN. On Monday, the newly enlarged company reported quarterly earnings for the first time and sketched out its plan for billions of dollars in cost savings. Ellison said in an earnings conference call with analysts that the streaming services will “converge” about a year from now. He promised to find at least $6 billion in “synergies” after combining Paramount with the much larger Warner. “By combining two global streaming services, two film and TV studio groups, two television portfolios, and overlapping corporate functions, we can reduce duplicative spend across an expense base of more than $50 billion,” the company said in a shareholder letter on Monday. Savings will come through layoffs, “reducing management layers,” consolidating real estate, streamlining the use of third-party vendors and relying more heavily on AI tools, among other areas. Ellison has already set up a leadership structure that unifies many of the far-flung Paramount and Warner brands under single leaders. And the changes are continuing. Skydance also announced Monday that James Gunn and Peter Safran would step down as co-chairmen of DC Studios and “return full time to their creative work.” Jeremy Latcham, a former Marvel executive, will replace them next month as head of the studio overseeing blockbuster franchises including Superman and Batman. Through the merger, every movie, TV episode and other piece of content “can work harder for us,” Monday’s shareholder letter stated, suggesting the titles can be distributed and monetized in new ways. A combined HBO Max-Paramount+ platform is critical to that. One of the first steps is to sell them together at a discounted price, though Skydance did not share pricing details on Monday. “Skydance’s plans to bundle Paramount+ and HBO Max is a temporary setup to get viewers accustomed with both offerings before they combine into a single entity,” Emarketer senior analyst Ross Benes said.

articles.title: Trump says FBI is investigating Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with alleged Chinese spy
articles.summary: The president said he spoke with Jensen Huang, who told him, “He had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy.”
articles.body: President Donald Trump said he spoke to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang earlier Monday after Nvidia revealed late Sunday that it had launched an investigation into his extramarital affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. Trump called Huang “to see if he’s feeling all right,” he said at an impromptu news briefing. “He had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy,” Trump said of Huang, adding, “I really believe him.” “We’ll look into it,” Trump said. “I know the FBI is looking into it, in terms of something else, and I think that he’ll be in good shape.” The Justice Department is conducting a criminal investigation into Megaspeed, the Singaporean company suspected of smuggling Nvidia’s artificial intelligence chips into China, according to a source familiar with the matter. Megaspeed is the data center company at the heart of the controversy involving Huang, who is said to have had a relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, the woman whom U.S. intelligence officials now believe to be a Chinese spy. Jensen Huang and Alice Huang are not related. The investigation is focused on allegations that Megaspeed played a role in shipping Nvidia AI computer chips to customers in China, which would violate strict U.S. export controls on those chips. In addition to Megaspeed, the probe is looking at people tied to the company, like Alice Huang, and at whether China recruited her to spy and assist the smuggling of the AI chips into China. The investigation is being led by the department’s National Security Division, in conjunction with the FBI and the Bureau of Industry and Security, the investigative division of the Commerce Department. On Sunday, the Nvidia board announced it was “initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” At the same time, Jensen Huang announced that he had been “unfaithful to my wife,” while also apologizing to Nvidia employees. “I was amazed, because I view him as a very high-quality person,” Trump told reporters at the White House. “He’s an amazing guy. I hope there’s no problem.” Trump indicated for the second time in as many days that he wanted Huang to remain the leader of Nvidia, the second-largest public company in the world. “I hope there’s no problem. If there is a problem, we’ll let you know about it. But I hope there’s no problem.” Nvidia spokespeople did not immediately reply to a request for comment Monday following Trump’s remarks. Nvidia previously said Huang would remain CEO, despite the revelations. The Justice Department also declined to comment on the matter. Chinese Foreign Affairs Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Monday that “the so-called Chinese spy allegation is unsubstantiated. It is nothing but smears against China.” Shares of Nvidia closed down 4.2% in Monday’s trading, bucking overall market momentum. The stock was the worst performer company in the Dow and the Nasdaq. The news surrounding Nvidia and Huang has also drawn intense congressional scrutiny. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., called Monday for “a full briefing” on the issues engulfing Nvidia. Jeffries is likely to be elected the next speaker of the House in January. Sens. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., and Jim Banks, R-Ind., also said in a joint statement that Congress should “take decisive action” regarding oversight of AI-linked companies. The news from Nvidia and Huang “makes these national security concerns even more urgent and raises important questions NVIDIA must answer,” Warren and Banks wrote.

articles.body:
Wyden says ‘lot of interest’ in raising Social Security cap

Democratic Sen. Ron Wyden (Ore.) said Monday that lawmakers have “a lot” of interest in raising the Social Security payroll tax cap to shore up the program’s funding base.

“There’s already a lot of interest, and some are starting to pop up on the other side of the aisle for raising the cap. So, we’ll be very involved in that,” Wyden, the incoming chair of the Senate Finance Committee, told reporters on Capitol Hill.

Officials from the Trump administration warned earlier this year that Social Security’s Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund will only cover the entirety of scheduled benefits until the final quarter of 2032. Starting then, the fund will cover 78 percent of scheduled benefits.

Taxpayers must pay Social Security taxes on up to $184,500 in income, an amount the Social Security Administration typically increases every year.

Sens. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) and Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) backed raising the Social Security tax cap over the summer, calling it a “common-sense solution” to the program’s impending funding issues.

“This is a no-brainer: The wealthiest Americans, who have benefited the most from America’s opportunities, should contribute the same percentage of their income as a factory worker in Chillicothe, Ohio, or a teacher in Worcester, Mass.,” they wrote in a New York Times opinion piece.

While speaking to reporters, Wyden also pushed for Congress to pass Medicare for All legislation and restrictions on chip exports to China — after the board of Nvidia opened a probe into a reported affair the company’s CEO, Jensen Huang , had with an alleged Chinese spy.

The Oregon Democrat specifically focused on healthcare costs, calling the country’s healthcare system “broken.”

Wyden added, “We’re going to be looking at big pharma and big insurance very closely, because both of them, particularly the big insurance companies, have just gotten a ride.”

articles.title: AI is not popular right now, but the US has to lead: Sierra co-founder Bret Taylor
articles.summary: Sierre cofounder Bret Taylor says the US must lead in AI.
articles.body:
Last week's midterm election results have been interpreted as a referendum on AI data centers, but despite pushback, Sierra co-founder and OpenAI chair Bret Taylor told Deirdre Bosa that the US needs to lead in the space.

"I would say building data centers was on the ballot. I think it's really an imperative in this country we lead in AI," Taylor said.

"And that means leading in power. It means leading in compute. It means leading in chips. It means leading in models, and then where we sit on the stack, leading in applied AI as well," he added.

Americans across the country have been protesting data centers over concerns about the facilities' impact on noise pollution, electricity rates, and the environment.

Last Tuesday's election saw Democrats take control of both houses of Congress, with many siding with the protesters. President Trump has strongly backed the data center build-out.

The election results sent shares of AI stocks plunging .

Sierra co-founder Clay Bavor, however, says there's room for debate about the technology and data centers.

"I think there's just going to be unbounded demand for high-quality intelligence and therefore compute," he said.

"I think there are all sorts of benefits of these data centers with jobs, training new folks in manufacturing and service, tax benefits. And also it's completely reasonable to be concerned about whether it's the noise or electricity bills and so on. So I think you can debate where to end up," Bavor added.

Taylor says the country will navigate the risks to the AI build-out, saying that the technology is too important.

"Big picture, I'm really bullish. I think we will navigate the risk. I don't know how. I mean, who knows what will come out tomorrow? But I think we'll navigate it because there's so much economic value in it," he said.

articles.title: Inflation likely took a breather last month as fuel prices fell
articles.summary: Tuesday’s CPI report will be the first snapshot of U.S. price growth since inflation-weary Americans voted for a Democratic sweep in the midterms.
articles.body: Americans are tired of inflation, as last week’s election results showed, but there may have been some relief last month as gasoline, diesel and jet fuel prices eased. The consumer price index, which is scheduled for release at 8:30 a.m. ET on Tuesday, is expected to show an increase of 0.3% month-over-month, according to a survey of economists conducted by Bloomberg. Economists also project that so-called core inflation, which does not include food or energy prices, rose 0.2%. In September, the CPI report showed prices grew 0.6% from August along with a 3.7% increase from a year earlier. (The October data will not include a year-ago number after the U.S. government shutdown disrupted the agency’s data collection, forcing it to skip the October 2025 CPI report entirely.) Even with some relief, the October data is set to illustrate the price pressures on consumers — a big factor in the Democrats’ sweeping victories in the congressional midterm elections last week. Eighty-four percent of voters told NBC News’ Exit Poll that they believed higher prices were a result of President Donald Trump’s policies, and 39% said the economy was their No. 1 issue at the ballot box, according to the exit poll. Those policies include global tariffs that add to the cost of products imported into the United States, as well as the war in Iran. Launched in February, that conflict has driven regular gas prices up 40%. Diesel fuel prices are 70% higher than at the start of the year. That, in turn, pushed inflation higher across the U.S.. Economists have warned that the rise in this commercial fuel can quickly ripple across the economy. Diesel is a major input cost for the transportation industry that delivers goods, such as groceries, to store shelves around the world. Gas prices declined last month, as Americans either voted early or geared up to cast their ballots on Election Day. On Oct. 1, the AAA national gas price average was $4.41 per gallon. At the end of the month, it was $4.18, a more than 5% drop. As a result, Citigroup economists predicted that Tuesday’s data will show “stabilizing and falling airfares, and limited pass through of higher energy costs into goods prices.” They also said shelter inflation and services prices could also show some slowing. Gas prices have continued trending downward in November, falling to $4 on Monday — although it’s still significantly higher than before the Iran war. Even as the oil price surge takes a breather, it may not last long. Throughout the Iran war, countries that are members of the International Energy Agency have released 400 million barrels of crude and related products, such as diesel, into the global market. “Restocking those inventories will create a floor under prices once the current conflict in the Middle East has faded,” said Diane Swonk, chief economist at KPMG. Given inflation’s overall stubbornness, economists believe the Federal Reserve will remain on track to hike rates for the second time this year. The Fed’s next two-day interest rate meeting will take place Dec. 8-9, right before the next inflation reading on Dec. 10. Market odds for a December hike sat at 85% Monday afternoon. “Still, details of Q4 data will be important for shifting inflation risks into 2027,” Citi economists wrote. Bank of America economists agreed, predicting that the report would be “a cooler start to fall,” after multiple months of rising inflation. Meanwhile, AI is also stoking inflation in other parts of the economy. In August, JPMorgan estimated that memory costs were on track to rise more than 400% from the end of 2024 through the end of 2026. Tech companies are spending hundreds of billions of dollars on data centers and the equipment that fills those facilities, pushing memory prices higher. Those costs are being passed down to consumers. Consumer tech companies, including Apple, have raised their prices as a result.

articles.title: Social Security tax by state: Where your benefits are and aren't taxed
articles.summary: Social Security benefits can be taxable at both the state and federal level. Learn which states tax benefits and what you can do to reduce your tax bill.
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

Whether your Social Security benefits are taxable depends on how much income you receive each year and where you live. Most states don't tax Social Security, but the federal government can still tax part of your benefits if your income exceeds certain limits.

Not everyone pays federal income taxes on their Social Security benefits. Just over half of beneficiaries will owe federal taxes on their benefits in 2026, according to the Congressional Budget Office.

Whether you will be taxed depends on your total income, including income from pensions, retirement accounts, and other sources.

The IRS uses a formula called "combined income" to determine how much of your benefits are taxable.

To calculate your combined income, add up:

Half your annual Social Security benefits

Your adjusted gross income, which includes wages, pensions, and taxable retirement withdrawals

Once you know your combined income, you can figure out how much of your Social Security benefits may be subject to federal taxes.

If you're married filing separately, the rules are different. If you lived with your spouse at any point during the year, you could owe taxes on up to 85% of your benefits regardless of how much income you receive. If you lived apart for the entire year, the $25,000 threshold applies.

Regardless of your filing status, how much you actually owe depends on your federal tax bracket and any deductions or credits you qualify for.

"Social Security income has always been partially tax-free," said Luke Delorme, a CFP and director of financial planning at Tableaux Wealth. "Even at high income levels, only 85% of Social Security benefits are taxable."

Not sure if your Social Security benefit is taxable? The IRS offers a free tool you can use to find out.

The 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act didn't actually eliminate taxes on Social Security or change the combined income thresholds, which haven't been increased since 1994.

Instead, the sweeping tax bill signed into law by President Trump introduced an additional deduction for people 65 and older worth up to $6,000 per person, or $12,000 for a married couple filing jointly if both spouses qualify. The deduction is available in tax years 2025 through 2028.

The deduction phases out once modified adjusted gross income surpasses $75,000 for individual filers or $150,000 for joint filers.

Depending on how much other income you have, that deduction could eliminate the taxes you owe on your benefits — or simply reduce your tax bill.

According to the White House, the new deduction moves the share of seniors who effectively owe nothing on their benefits from about 64% to about 88%.

But why not just eliminate federal taxes on Social Security? "The new deduction isn't as costly," said Delorme.

Completely eliminating federal taxes on Social Security benefits would have cost an estimated $1.4 trillion over 10 years, compared with about $93 billion for the senior deduction that passed, according to the Bipartisan Policy Center.

Where you live can also affect how much of your Social Security is taxable.

The good news is only eight states still tax Social Security benefits in 2026. Even then, you might not owe anything since nearly all states offer tax breaks based on your income, age, or both.

For example, New Mexico exempts Social Security benefits from state income taxes if your adjusted gross income is $100,000 or less as a single filer, or $150,000 or less if you're married filing jointly.

Here's how all 50 states and Washington, D.C., tax Social Security benefits in 2026.

Ages 55-64: fully exempt with AGI of $75,000 or less (single) or $95,000 or less (joint)

Above those limits, up to $20,000 can be deducted

Fully exempt with AGI below $75,000 (single) or $100,000 (joint)

Above those limits, no more than 25% of benefits are taxable

Fully exempt with AGI of $86,410 or less (single) or $110,780 or less (joint). Exemptions phase out above those limits as income rises.

Federally taxable benefits are subject to state income tax.

Fully exempt with AGI of $100,000 or less (single) or $150,000 or less (joint)

No Social Security exemption above those limits

Total exemption if you've reached full retirement age and your federal AGI is below the state's income limits, which are adjusted annually for inflation

Starting in 2027, total exemption for eligible retirees who haven't reached full retirement age yet

Tax credit can offset state tax on benefits

Credit phases out when income exceeds $54,000 (single), $90,000 (joint or head of household), or $45,000 (married filing separately)

Fully exempt with AGI of $55,000 or less (single) or $70,000 or less (joint)

Partial exemption for AGI up to $65,000 (single) or $80,000 (joint).

Wondering how much Social Security you'll receive in retirement?

Our Social Security calculator can help you estimate how much you'll receive per month based on your earnings history and when you plan to claim benefits. Once you know your estimated benefits, you can figure out any potential taxes you might owe.

Most states have moved away from taxing Social Security benefits in recent years.

West Virginia began phasing out the tax for higher-income earners in 2024, letting residents deduct 35% of their taxable benefits that year and 65% in 2025. As of 2026, all Social Security benefits are exempt from West Virginia income taxes, regardless of how much you earn.

Kansas, Missouri, and Nebraska also made changes that took effect in 2024. Kansas and Missouri eliminated income limits that prevented higher-earning retirees from qualifying for a full Social Security tax break. Meanwhile, Nebraska accelerated its phaseout, which began in 2021, eventually eliminating the tax entirely in 2024, three years ahead of schedule.

Starting in 2027, Rhode Island will stop taxing Social Security benefits for eligible retirees who haven't reached their full retirement age yet. Previously, you had to meet both age and income requirements to qualify for an exemption. The change is expected to help about 9,200 Rhode Islanders save on taxes.

Meanwhile, Connecticut and Vermont considered broader Social Security exemptions in 2026, but neither bill became law, so the current exemption rules remain in effect.

You can't change IRS rules, but there are a few ways to lower your income and potentially reduce the taxes you owe on your Social Security benefits.

Be strategic about retirement withdrawals: Taking a big chunk out of your traditional IRA or 401(k) in a single year could increase the taxes you owe on your Social Security benefits. Spreading out withdrawals over several years can help lower your tax bill.

Draw from a Roth IRA: Unlike traditional retirement accounts, qualified Roth IRA withdrawals don't count toward the income used to determine whether your Social Security benefits are taxable. So if you need extra money one year, tapping your Roth IRA instead of a traditional IRA or 401(k) could help reduce your tax bill.

Watch your investment income: Selling stocks or other investments for a profit in a brokerage account can increase your taxable income, which could also make more of your Social Security benefits taxable. Even interest from tax-free municipal bonds counts when the IRS calculates your combined income for Social Security taxes.

Take advantage of tax breaks: If you're 65 or older, you may qualify for the new federal senior tax deduction. Many states also offer exemptions or tax credits that can reduce what you owe on your benefits.

Have taxes taken out of your checks: If you think you might owe federal taxes, you can ask Social Security to withhold money from your monthly payments. This won't save you money on taxes, but it can help you avoid getting stuck with a big bill when you file your return.

Before making a large retirement withdrawal or moving money from a traditional IRA to a Roth IRA, consider talking to a tax professional who can explain how the move might impact your Social Security taxes.

Most states won't tax your Social Security benefits, but federal taxes can still apply. It's important to check the rules at both the state and federal levels before assuming your entire monthly paycheck is yours to keep.

Turning 70 doesn't trigger a special federal exemption. You'll still use the same combined income rules to determine if your Social Security benefits are taxable, though the new additional senior deduction could lower your tax bill through 2028.

In eight states, at least some federally taxable benefits can count toward state taxable income. Elsewhere, states exempt benefits or don't levy an income tax.

Not necessarily. Each state sets its own rules for pensions, IRAs, and workplace retirement plans. And a state that exempts Social Security, such as California, may still tax withdrawals from your 401(k).

There's no federal law in place to stop taxing Social Security in 2027. On the state level, Rhode Island's exemption expands that year, but qualifying higher-income residents can still owe state tax.

Yes, if you establish residency in a state that doesn't tax benefits. But moving won't erase federal taxes.

articles.title: Trump Media cashes in on high-speed access to social media posts
articles.summary: The firm’s revenue jumped more than 200% after it started selling a direct feed of posts from Truth Social, whose most prominent user is President Trump.
articles.body: Trump Media and Technology Group reported Monday that revenue surged 205% in the third quarter, which it says was “primarily driven” by selling a high-speed feed of posts on Truth Social. The “Truth API,” as the company calls it, allows news organizations, Wall Street trading firms and other services to pay $60,000 to $100,000 per month for a direct feed of posts on the social network. Critics have slammed the feed as an attempt to profit from President Donald Trump’s posts. Trump, whose revocable trust is the largest single shareholder of Trump Media, is the most prominent user of Truth Social. Trump’s trust owns more than 41% of Trump Media, according to S&P Capital IQ data. In a June filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, the trust said Donald Trump Jr. was “the sole trustee and has sole voting and investment power” over its holdings. Trump Media’s stock, which trades under the symbol DJT for Trump’s initials, closed at $4.06 on Monday, giving it a market valuation of $1.13 billion. It’s down 69% so far this year. In July, Trump Media announced the high-speed feed offering, saying it would allow “real-time access to posts from the highest-ranking Truth Social accounts.” The company acknowledged that the service could be market-moving and highly valuable to any trading firm. “Markets already move on Truth Social posts,” Kevin McGurn, interim CEO of Trump Media, said at the time. He added that “high frequency and algorithmic trading firms that require a low-latency, machine-readable feed rather than manual tracking” could benefit from paying for the feed. In August, the company said the service had gone live. Last month, Reuters reported that Bloomberg and two Wall Street trading firms were some of the customers who had signed up for the service. Bloomberg declined to comment to NBC News in October, while the two other firms did not reply to requests for comment at the time. Two top Democratic senators, Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts and Adam Schiff of California, said the Truth Social feed amounts to “an outrageous abuse of the President’s office for his personal benefit.” In July, they asked the SEC to “determine whether the proposed arrangement would violate applicable federal securities laws.” Trump was asked Sunday whether he was using the presidency to enrich himself. “I devote almost no time to my net worth,” Trump told CBS News’ “60 Minutes” in an interview. “I have a lot of money, and far more than I ever thought I’d have. And I guess it’s gone up. I don’t even know.” Trump said his son “watches over” his money, adding: “I don’t even talk to him about it.” Trump’s personal finances differ vastly from those of other recent presidents. In June, Trump’s most recent personal financial disclosure ran more than 900 pages. By comparison, President Barack Obama’s final disclosure form was eight pages, while President Joe Biden’s was 11. Vice President JD Vance’s form for last year is 17 pages. Trump’s disclosure shows billions of dollars in earnings tied to cryptocurrencies, media settlements and vast personal investments in stocks and bonds. The White House has repeatedly insisted that “neither the President nor his family has ever engaged — or will ever engage — in conflicts of interest.”

articles.title: Jensen Huang reportedly engaged a PR firm with a history of handling  high-profile sex scandals a year ago
articles.summary: The PR firm was enlisted shortly after an October 2025 New York Times report described Alice Huang's business dealings with Jensen Huang, Wired reported.
articles.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang hired Heller Inc., a crisis communications firm known for handling sex scandals, at least a year before he publicly acknowledged an extramarital affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, Wired reported .

Heller Inc. founder Risa Heller has advised prominent men through personal scandals and sexual misconduct accusations, according to a 2023 New York Magazine profile. Her reported clients include former congressman Anthony Weiner , celebrity chef Mario Batali , and former New Yorker writer Jeffrey Toobin.

Wired also reported that Nvidia's internal communications team was told to copy Heller Inc. on press inquiries about Huang shortly after an October 2025 New York Times report about whether Nvidia was helping Chinese companies evade U.S. chip export restrictions.

The Times reported that Megaspeed, a then little-known Singapore-based data center company with ties to China, had acquired nearly $2 billion worth of Nvidia chips. It described Megaspeed CEO Alice Huang, the woman later linked to Jensen Huang, standing next to him at a Taipei gathering of Nvidia customers.

Heller and Nvidia didn't immediately respond to requests for comment.

On Sunday, Nvidia published a statement from Huang acknowledging an affair with a former Megaspeed executive, though he didn't name Alice Huang. Nvidia's board separately announced an independent investigation, citing reports that Huang "has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort."

articles.title: More Gen Zs are Ditching Entry-Level Jobs to Start Businesses Relying Heavily on AI
articles.summary: Young Americans are increasingly choosing entrepreneurship over traditional corporate jobs, according to a new report.
articles.body:
A growing number of young Americans are choosing to start businesses instead of following the traditional path from college to an entry-level corporate job. And with artificial intelligence making it cheaper and easier to get started , some are building companies before gaining much experience in the workplace.

About 23% of Americans ages 18 to 34 ran a business or side project in 2025, up from 19% in 2021, according to research from Babson College's Global Entrepreneurship Monitor. Among those aged 18 to 24, entrepreneurial activity has more than doubled over the past decade.

The interest is particularly strong among Gen Z, which accounted for 9% of new business starts in 2025, compared with 5% for Baby Boomers, according to a 2026 report from payroll provider Gusto. It was the first time Gen Z entrepreneurs started more businesses than Boomers, although the younger generation still owns only a small share of all existing businesses.

That interest is showing up in broader surveys, too. Some 43% of Gen Z respondents were considering starting a business in 2026, compared with 39% of millennials and 21% of Gen X, according to research from Intuit QuickBooks.

For many younger Americans, the attraction goes beyond the possibility of making more money. Business ownership offers greater control over working hours, career decisions and future opportunities, without having to climb the corporate ladder.

One of the biggest changes is the growing availability of AI tools that can take on work traditionally requiring outside professionals or additional employees.

Gusto found that 71% of Gen Z entrepreneurs who launched businesses in 2025 used AI during the startup process, compared with 42% of Baby Boomer founders. More than two-thirds of young entrepreneurs said the technology made starting their businesses faster and less expensive.

AI was used for developing business ideas, handling administrative work and setting up operations. More than half of Gen Z founders surveyed used it to help generate business ideas.

The technology is also becoming more common among business owners generally. Across all generations, AI adoption among new businesses increased from 21% in 2023 to 44% in 2025, according to Gusto.

But the businesses young Americans are starting are not necessarily technology companies. In fact, Gusto's July 2026 research, based on payroll data from more than 500,000 small businesses and a survey of 1,051 founders, found that Gen Z entrepreneurs were more than twice as likely as older business owners to operate in-person businesses.

articles.title: Área técnica da Aneel propõe detalhar na conta de luz horários de maior e menor consumo; entenda | G1
articles.standfirst: Modalidade será voltada para consumidores de baixa tensão que usam mais de 500 quilowatts-hora (kWh) por mês. Cerca de 5,7 milhões de unidades consumidoras se enquadram nesse perfil.
articles.summary: Modalidade será voltada para consumidores de baixa tensão que usam mais de 500 quilowatts-hora (kWh) por mês. Cerca de 5,7 milhões de unidades consumidoras se enquadram nesse perfil.
articles.body:
A área técnica da Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) está na fase final de elaboração da chamada "tarifa hora certa", proposta na qual a conta de luz passe a variar de acordo com o horário de consumo.

A ideia é estimular o uso da eletricidade fora dos horários de maior demanda e, com isso, reduzir custos.

Para entrar em vigor, a medida ainda precisa ser aprovada pela diretoria da agência. A expectativa é que a análise ocorra em dezembro.

A nova modalidade será voltada para consumidores de baixa tensão que usam mais de 500 quilowatts-hora (kWh) por mês. Segundo cálculos da Aneel, cerca de 5,7 milhões de unidades consumidoras se enquadram nesse perfil.

Na prática, o público atingido deve ser formado principalmente por pequenos comércios e indústrias de menor porte. Isso porque o consumo médio das residências brasileiras é de cerca de 160 kWh mensais, segundo técnicos da agência.

A tarifa hora certa é uma reformulação da tarifa branca, modalidade criada em 2018 que cobra valores diferentes pelo quilowatt-hora (kWh) de acordo com o horário e o dia da semana em que a energia é consumida.

Hoje, a adesão à tarifa branca é voluntária . A modalidade não se popularizou e reúne cerca de 69 mil unidades consumidoras após oito anos de funcionamento.

A principal mudança na nova proposta é que a migração passará a ser automática para os consumidores que se enquadrarem nos critérios estabelecidos pela Aneel até se tornar obrigatória.

💡A proposta prevê a criação de três classificações de horário:

intermediário, que corresponde normalmente a uma hora antes e uma hora depois do pico;

e fora de pico, que inclui madrugada, fins de semana e feriados.

A implementação será gradual. Consumidores com maior consumo serão os primeiros a ingressar no novo modelo. Antes da entrada em cada fase, as distribuidoras terão de informar aos clientes como ficaria a conta de luz caso a tarifa hora certa já estivesse em vigor.

O consumidor poderá optar por deixar a modalidade durante o período de transição. Caso não se manifeste, será automaticamente incluído no novo sistema.

Quem decidir não aderir pode optar pela modalidade chamada "tarifa plana temporária". Nela, o valor da energia é calculado com base nos custos dos horários de ponta, quando a eletricidade é mais cara.

Segundo estimativas da Aneel, essa opção deve resultar em uma conta entre 3% e 5% mais alta do que a tarifa hora certa.

O período de adaptação termina em 2033 quando a tarifa plana temporária deixa de existir. Ou seja: todos os consumidores acima de 500 kwh/mês serão incluídos na tarifa horária.

Após esse período, a proposta prevê três etapas de implementação:

Abril de 2028 : consumidores com uso superior a 1.800 kWh/mês;

Abril de 2029 : consumidores com uso superior a 1.000 kWh/mês;

Abril de 2031 : consumidores com uso superior a 500 kWh/mês.

Segundo a Aneel, os consumidores receberão, com pelo menos três meses de antecedência, uma simulação de quanto pagariam na tarifa hora certa e poderão solicitar a saída do modelo antes da mudança entra em vigor.

Conta de energia no RN — Foto: Divulgação/Neoenergia Cosern

Beneficiários da Tarifa Social de Energia Elétrica;

Unidades com sistema pré-pago de energia.

Consumidores que usam menos de 500 kWh por mês continuarão na tarifa convencional, mas poderão aderir voluntariamente à nova modalidade, desde que possuam medidor compatível.

A proposta dos técnicos afirma que a tarifa hora certa não cria um novo custo para o consumidor, mas torna mais visível a diferença de preço da energia ao longo do dia.

Unidades com painéis solares seguem as mesmas regras dos demais consumidores e poderão pedir para sair da modalidade durante o período de transição.

Novos projetos de geração própria, novas unidades que recebam créditos de energia dessas usinas e novas estações comerciais de recarga de veículos elétricos entrarão na tarifa hora certa 90 dias após a publicação da norma, sem possibilidade de saída.

A substituição do medidor será feita pelas distribuidoras. Apenas unidades equipadas com aparelhos capazes de registrar o consumo por horário poderão ser migradas automaticamente.

articles.title: Gás do Povo: quem recebe o voucher de novembro e como consultar | G1
articles.standfirst: Benefício garante a recarga gratuita de botijão de 13 kg em revendas credenciadas.
articles.summary: Benefício garante a recarga gratuita de botijão de 13 kg em revendas credenciadas.
articles.body:
'Gás do Povo': recarga gratuita de botijão começa na segunda (24) em Teresina; veja como vai funcionar — Foto: Divulgação

O voucher do Gás do Povo de novembro será disponibilizado nesta terça-feira (10) para as famílias que têm direito ao benefício. O programa garante a recarga gratuita de um botijão de gás de cozinha de 13 kg em revendas credenciadas.

A distribuição dos vales ocorre sempre no dia 10 de cada mês , segundo o calendário da Caixa.

O benefício, no entanto, não é liberado necessariamente para todas as famílias todos os meses. A frequência depende da quantidade de pessoas que compõem a família registrada no Cadastro Único (CadÚnico).

Famílias com 2 ou 3 pessoas recebem um vale a cada três meses. Já aquelas com 4 pessoas ou mais recebem um vale a cada dois meses.

É possível consultar se há um voucher disponível informando o CPF do responsável familiar no site oficial do Gás do Povo , mantido pelo Ministério do Desenvolvimento e Assistência Social (MDS).

Na página de consulta, basta informar o CPF do responsável familiar cadastrado no CadÚnico para verificar a situação do benefício.

A situação também pode ser consultada por outros canais, como o aplicativo Meu Social, o aplicativo Benefícios Sociais CAIXA e o Portal Cidadão da Caixa.

Para participar do programa, a família precisa estar inscrita no CadÚnico, com os dados atualizados nos últimos 24 meses, e ter renda familiar mensal de até meio salário mínimo por pessoa.

Também é necessário que o CPF do responsável familiar esteja regularizado na Receita Federal e que a família não esteja em situação de averiguação cadastral ou com indício de óbito do responsável familiar no CadÚnico.

A seleção das famílias é feita de acordo com os critérios do programa. Portanto, estar inscrito no CadÚnico e atender aos requisitos não significa necessariamente que haverá um voucher disponível em cada rodada.

Não. O Gás do Povo não deposita um valor em dinheiro na conta do beneficiário.

O programa oferece uma recarga gratuita de um botijão de gás de cozinha de 13 kg. O responsável familiar deve utilizar o vale em uma revenda credenciada pelo programa.

Depois de confirmar que tem direito ao benefício, o responsável familiar deve procurar uma revenda credenciada.

A validação pode ser feita de três formas:

cartão do Bolsa Família com chip e senha;

cartão de débito de uma conta da Caixa e senha;

CPF do responsável familiar e código de validação enviado por SMS para o celular cadastrado na Caixa.

No caso do uso do CPF, é importante manter o número de celular atualizado no CAIXA Tem para receber o código de validação.

Sim. O programa permite escolher entre retirar a recarga na revenda ou solicitar a entrega em casa, desde que a revenda ofereça esse serviço.

A recarga do botijão é gratuita, mas pode haver cobrança pela entrega. Também pode haver custo caso a família não disponibilize um vasilhame vazio no momento da troca.

Quando será o próximo voucher do Gás do Povo?

A Caixa prevê a disponibilização dos vales no dia 10 de cada mês. Depois de setembro, o calendário prevê novas liberações em 10 de outubro, 10 de novembro e 10 de dezembro de 2026.

Isso não significa, porém, que uma mesma família receberá um voucher em todas essas datas. A periodicidade depende da composição familiar e da permanência nos critérios do programa.

articles.title: O futuro da economia brasileira no quarto mandato de Lula - O Assunto #1842 | G1
articles.standfirst: Em primeiro pronunciamento após a reeleição, presidente sinaliza os rumos da política econômica a partir de janeiro de 2027.
articles.summary: Em primeiro pronunciamento após a reeleição, presidente sinaliza os rumos da política econômica a partir de janeiro de 2027.
articles.body:
Na noite de domingo (8), Lula fez seu primeiro pronunciamento oficial como presidente reeleito. Foi também a primeira sinalização mais clara sobre qual caminho irá tomar para a condução da política econômica. No dia seguinte ao resultado das urnas, o mercado financeiro reagiu mal: bolsa caiu, dólar subiu e a curva de juros embicou para cima. Agentes econômicos apontam que a incerteza sobre o encaminhamento da trajetória da dívida pública tem sido o principal fator de instabilidade. No discurso, Lula admitiu preocupação com a questão fiscal e com os altos juros brasileiros e afirmou que irá buscar equilibrar responsabilidade com as contas e investimento público.

Neste episódio, Victor Boyadjian recebe o economista e filósofo Eduardo Giannetti para uma entrevista sobre os rumos do país neste quarto mandato de Lula, que se inicia em 5 de janeiro de 2027. Giannetti comenta as medidas que acredita serem fundamentais para enfrentar os desafios de curto prazo, mas também analisa as possibilidades de projeto de país que se apresentam com mais investimento em economia verde e em capital humano.

Convidado: Professor Eduardo Giannetti, economista, filósofo, autor e membro da Academia Brasileira de Letras.

O podcast O Assunto é produzido por: Luiz Felipe Silva, Luiz Gabriel Franco, Juliene Moretti, Stéphanie Nascimento, Marco Antônio Martins e Thomé Granemann. Na apresentação: Natuza Nery.

articles.title: Reforma tributária muda regras para renda com aluguel; veja como fica para pessoas físicas e jurídicas | G1
articles.standfirst: A CBS e o IBS passarão a incidir sobre rendimentos vindos do aluguel, com regras distintas para proprietários que são PJ e PF. A nova cobrança será gradual, com gatilhos e fase de transição até 2029.
articles.summary: A CBS e o IBS passarão a incidir sobre rendimentos vindos do aluguel, com regras distintas para proprietários que são PJ e PF. A nova cobrança será gradual, com gatilhos e fase de transição até 2029.
articles.body:
O mercado de aluguel de imóveis no Brasil vai passar por mudanças com a reforma tributária . A renda obtida com aluguéis, que até agora era tributada apenas pelo Imposto de Renda, também será incluída na nova cobrança sobre o consumo.

O impacto, porém, não será igual para todos: tudo vai depender se o proprietário do imóvel é pessoa jurídica ou pessoa física — e, neste último caso, somente se certos “gatilhos” forem acionados.

💰 A aplicação da Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS) e do Imposto sobre Bens e Serviços (IBS) sobre os rendimentos vindos de aluguéis não será imediata. A CBS começará a valer em 2027 , enquanto o IBS só entrará em funcionamento em 2029 .

Entenda nesta reportagem como deve ficar a carga tributária para os proprietários, como funcionará o período de transição e quais medidas podem ajudar a reduzir o impacto dos custos para os inquilinos .

O que muda para o proprietário pessoa física?

Jaques Bushatsky, diretor de Legislação do Inquilinato da Secovi-SP (Sindicato da Habitação), ressalta que, até o momento, quem aluga imóveis como pessoa física paga apenas o Imposto de Renda (IRPF) sobre os rendimentos , com alíquotas progressivas que variam de 7,5% a 27,5%.

“A reforma, como está desenhada, prevê gatilhos que podem incluir a pessoa física na cobrança do IBS/CBS, eliminando a isenção atualmente existente [no PIS/COFINS] ou o tratamento simplificado no IRPF”, explica Bushatsky.

Esses gatilhos envolvem duas condições simultâneas:

⚠️ Receita anual com aluguel superior a R$ 240 mil (ou mais de R$ 20 mil por mês );

⚠️ Locação de três ou mais imóveis distintos.

Há ainda uma alternativa: mesmo que o limite de R$ 240 mil não tenha sido ultrapassado no ano anterior, se a receita com aluguel atingir R$ 288 mil no ano atual (20% acima do gatilho), o locador também será enquadrado no regime do IBS/CBS.

Florence Haret Drago, professora conferencista do Instituto Brasileiro de Estudos Tributários (IBET) e sócia da área tributária no NHM Advogados, explica que, caso o locador pessoa física não se enquadre nos critérios definidos, continuará pagando apenas o Imposto de Renda , sem incidência de tributos sobre o consumo.

Segundo ela, compreender como esse conceito será interpretado é essencial para pessoas físicas que utilizam a locação de imóveis como fonte de renda . “A proposta, até agora, não estabelece nova tributação sobre os valores recebidos por quem não exerce atividade empresarial.”

Para empresas que atuam com aluguel de imóveis — como holdings patrimoniais, incorporadoras ou companhias do setor imobiliário — a reforma tributária trará uma nova cobrança: a receita gerada com aluguéis passará a ser considerada prestação de serviço, sujeita à incidência de IBS/CBS.

Ou seja, o proprietário que for pessoa jurídica terá de arcar com uma tributação adicional sobre os valores recebidos com aluguel.

💲 Atualmente, uma pessoa jurídica que aluga imóveis paga tributos como IRPJ, CSLL, PIS e Cofins. No regime de lucro presumido, a carga tributária efetiva sobre aluguéis varia entre aproximadamente 11,33% e 14% . Já no regime de Lucro Real, a tributação incide sobre o lucro efetivamente apurado.

💲 Com o novo regime, estima-se que a alíquota combinada de IBS/CBS sobre essa receita fique entre 25% e 30%. Ao somar os tributos já existentes, como IRPJ e CSLL, o impacto bruto pode chegar a até 37,38% sobre a receita, antes da aplicação de créditos.

Apesar disso, a reforma prevê um alívio parcial por meio da não cumulatividade plena — permitindo que as empresas deduzam integralmente os tributos pagos ao longo de todas as etapas da produção, garantindo que a cobrança incida apenas sobre o valor agregado final.

Com isso, a Fazenda busca evitar o chamado “efeito cascata”, em que o imposto é cobrado repetidamente ao longo da cadeia. Na avaliação de especialistas tributários, esse crédito fiscal pode reduzir a carga efetiva entre 5 e 10 pontos percentuais .

“Isso significa que a empresa locadora poderá abater do imposto devido parte do IBS/CBS pago em despesas relacionadas à atividade, como manutenção e administração”, acrescenta Heitor Cesar Ribeiro, advogado tributarista e sócio do escritório Gaia Silva Gaede Advogados.

Segundo Jaques Bushatsky, as imobiliárias também serão tributadas pelo IBS/CBS, mas sobre a sua própria receita — que é a taxa de administração ou a comissão de corretagem.

“O aluguel em si não é receita da imobiliária, ele apenas transita pelo seu caixa para ser repassado ao proprietário. A base de cálculo do tributo da imobiliária é o serviço que ela presta, não o valor total do aluguel que ela administra”, completa o diretor de Legislação do Inquilinato da Secovi-SP.

Como a reforma tributária afeta os aluguéis — Foto: Arte/g1

Para moderar o impacto e suavizar o impacto da nova tributação sobre o setor de locação, a reforma também estabeleceu alguns mecanismos de atenuação e alívio. Sendo eles:

Redução de 70% na base de cálculo de IBS/CBS aplicáveis à locação — isto é, ao calcular o imposto de consumo sobre aluguéis, apenas 30% da base seria considerada.

Redutor social de R$ 600 mensais por unidade residencial , que diminui a base de cálculo para imóveis residenciais. Em casos extremos (aluguel residencial até R$ 600), pode não haver tributação adicional.

Segundo o Ministério da Fazenda , esses “ alívios ” foram pensados para preservar a locação residencial de menor valor e evitar que novas camadas tributárias tornem o mercado inviável para locadores moderados.

Para contratos já existentes (firmados até 16/01/2025), foi criado um regime opcional chamado de transição. Sob essa opção:

Locadores PF ou PJ podem optar por recolher 3,65% de CBS/IBS sobre a receita bruta, sem direito a créditos ou ao redutor social ;

Para contratos residenciais, a opção vale até o fim do contrato original ou até 31 de dezembro de 2028 , o que vier primeiro;

Para contratos não residenciais, vale pelo prazo original do contrato.

Na avaliação de João Pedro Ramos Garcia, sócio e especialista em tributação no escritório Ballstaedt Gasparino Advogados, o regime de transição funciona como uma “válvula de segurança” para contratos antigos — embora tenha um custo associado.

“A alíquota transitória de 3,65% pode servir como um amortecedor temporário para contratos antigos, mas elimina créditos e tem prazo definido para terminar, o que pode antecipar renegociações”, aponta o tributarista.

Por isso, essa opção nem sempre é a mais vantajosa para o proprietário — dependendo das despesas envolvidas e da estrutura adotada , o regime padrão com possibilidade de créditos pode representar menor custo.

Para ajudar quem ainda tem dúvidas sobre qual regime escolher, a Secovi-SP fez simulações comparativas. Confira:

Queda na rentabilidade ou repasse de valor

O diretor de Legislação do Inquilinato da Secovi-SP reconhece que, com a nova incidência de tributos de consumo, a margem líquida dos locadores tende a diminuir , especialmente para quem já atua com rentabilidade reduzida.

“Muitos proprietários podem sentir a necessidade de elevar o valor do aluguel para compensar a carga extra”, diz Bushatsky.

O repasse, no entanto, não será automático: ele dependerá das condições do mercado imobiliário local — como oferta e demanda, poder de negociação do imóvel, contratos já existentes e possibilidade de reajuste.

Além disso, os impactos também serão diferentes se o locatário for pessoa jurídica ou pessoa física.

Em aluguéis comerciais, o locatário PJ (empresa) poderá usar créditos do IBS/CBS embutido no aluguel , abater parte desse tributo do que já paga em suas próprias operações. Isso reduz o impacto real sobre o custo da locação.

➡️ OU SEJA: Mesmo que o aluguel inclua imposto, ele pode não ser um custo líquido, pois parte será “recuperada” no balanço da empresa.

Aqui reside o ponto mais sensível da reforma, na avaliação de Bushatsky: o locatário PF, considerado consumidor final, não terá direito a créditos do IBS/CBS .

"Não existe, no desenho atual da reforma, um mecanismo de compensação direta ou crédito para o locatário pessoa física. Ele não é contribuinte do imposto, é consumidor final", afirma o diretor da Secovi-SP.

➡️ Esse cenário pode gerar disparidades: famílias que alugam imóveis de empresas enfrentarão o impacto integral, enquanto empresas inquilinas poderão neutralizar parte do tributo via crédito.

A padronização cadastral via Cadastro Imobiliário Brasileiro (CIB) será parte da infraestrutura do novo sistema. A mudança traz novos deveres fiscais, e o descumprimento pode gerar sanções.

📝 Embora o CIB não crie tributos, ele servirá para cruzar dados e tornar a fiscalização mais eficiente. Por isso, divergências entre contrato, nota fiscal e cadastro inserido no CIB poderão ser motivos de autuação.

Emissão incorreta ou falta de nota fiscal eletrônica (NF-e) ou documento fiscal equivalente quando exigido;

Recolhimento incorreto (menor ou tardio) de CBS/IBS;

Mistura indevida de receitas que optaram e não optaram pela transição;

Falha em comprovar contratos elegíveis ou cumprir prazos de registro;

Inconsistências entre contratos, cadastros (ex: CIB) e notas fiscais.

Vale lembrar, ainda, que como as mudanças tributárias são fatores externos ao contrato, pode haver espaço para pedidos de revisão contratual , com base no artigo 317 do Código Civil e na chamada teoria da imprevisão .

“A jurisprudência dos tribunais reconhece que fatos inesperados e relevantes — como mudanças legislativas significativas, incluindo alterações tributárias — podem justificar a revisão contratual, quando tornam a execução excessivamente onerosa para uma das partes”, ressalta Florence Haret Drago.

articles.title: Superávit comercial da China supera US$ 1 trilhão com foco em IA | G1
articles.standfirst: Exportações cresceram 35,2% em outubro, impulsionadas pela demanda global por produtos de alta tecnologia; avanço pode ampliar tensões comerciais com União Europeia e EUA.
articles.summary: O superávit comercial da China superou US$ 1 trilhão com o salto nas exportações para IA, compensando a crise interna e elevando tensões comerciais com EUA e Europa.
articles.body:
Vista do horizonte da cidade Shenzhen, na China. — Foto: Tingshu Wang/Reuters

O superávit comercial da China ultrapassou US$ 1 trilhão nos primeiros dez meses do ano , à medida que a corrida global para construir infraestrutura de inteligência artificial impulsionou as vendas de produtos de alta tecnologia e ajudou a compensar a fraca demanda interna, uma dinâmica que provavelmente aumentará as tensões com os principais parceiros comerciais.

Os números destacam a crescente dependência de Pequim da demanda externa para sustentar uma economia prejudicada pelo consumo fraco e por uma prolongada crise no setor imobiliário. Embora se espere que o boom global de investimentos em IA mantenha forte a demanda por produtos tecnológicos chineses até 2027, ele corre o risco de aprofundar os desequilíbrios internos e alimentar atritos comerciais com parceiros, incluindo a União Europeia.

As exportações cresceram expressivos 35,2% em outubro em relação ao mesmo mês do ano anterior, em termos de dólares americanos, mostraram dados da alfândega nesta terça-feira. O avanço ficou apenas ligeiramente abaixo da alta de 36,3% registrada em setembro, mas superou a previsão dos economistas, que esperavam crescimento de 33,5%.

Isso ajudou a elevar o superávit comercial da China para US$ 1,04 trilhão nos primeiros dez meses do ano, superando US$ 1 trilhão pelo segundo ano consecutivo e atingindo essa marca um mês antes do que em 2025.

O aumento do superávit pode alimentar novas tensões com a União Europeia, onde líderes têm defendido mais restrições comerciais contra a China após chegarem a um acordo com Pequim para limitar as exportações chinesas de veículos híbridos ao bloco nos próximos anos. Como as medidas ainda não entraram em vigor, espera-se que as fábricas antecipem os embarques, fortalecendo as exportações no curto prazo.

A China anunciou oficialmente na segunda-feira a prorrogação por dois meses de uma trégua comercial com Washington que venceria em 10 de novembro, mas afirmou na semana passada que a ampliação das compras de produtos agrícolas dos Estados Unidos dependeria da implementação do acordo de redução recíproca de tarifas firmado entre os dois países.

“O risco de tarifas adicionais e outras barreiras comerciais continuará elevado em 2027, especialmente à medida que os fabricantes chineses continuarem expandindo sua presença nos mercados externos”, disse Joe Peissel, economista-chefe para macroeconomia da Trivium China.

Diante desse cenário, as importações cresceram 41,6% em outubro em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior, superando a previsão mediana de alta de 32% em pesquisa da Reuters e acelerando em relação ao crescimento de 31% registrado em setembro.

O superávit comercial da China com os Estados Unidos caiu ligeiramente , para US$ 32,71 bilhões em outubro, ante US$ 34,01 bilhões no mês anterior, mas o elevado desequilíbrio continua sendo um ponto de atrito entre as duas potências econômicas.

As importações de petróleo caíram 13,3% em relação ao ano anterior, embora os embarques tenham atingido o maior nível desde março, à medida que compradores buscaram suprimentos após a guerra entre Estados Unidos e Israel contra o Irã afetar os fluxos de petróleo do Oriente Médio.

Xi Jinping e Donald Trump se reuniram nos Estados Unidos no final de setembro — Foto: Bloomberg via Getty Images

Os dados comerciais foram divulgados antes da cúpula da Cooperação Econômica Ásia-Pacífico (Apec), que acontecerá na próxima semana em Shenzhen, onde o presidente chinês, Xi Jinping, e o presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, devem se reunir pela terceira vez neste ano, colocando as tensões comerciais e a política tarifária no centro das atenções.

Após uma cúpula entre Xi e Trump realizada em setembro , em Washington, os dois lados propuseram um pacote de US$ 60 bilhões em reduções recíprocas de tarifas , incluindo cerca de US$ 17 bilhões em produtos agrícolas dos Estados Unidos.

Uma grande preocupação para Pequim é que os consumidores continuam relutantes em gastar, limitados por uma crise no mercado imobiliário que atingiu duramente o patrimônio das famílias e abalou a confiança nas perspectivas econômicas.

A fraca demanda interna levou as montadoras chinesas a buscar vendas nos mercados externos. As exportações de automóveis da China mantiveram um ritmo sólido de crescimento em outubro, enquanto as vendas de veículos no mercado interno registraram o 12º mês consecutivo de queda, segundo dados separados divulgados por uma associação do setor.

A maior dependência das exportações, no entanto, deixa a economia chinesa cada vez mais exposta a uma eventual desaceleração da demanda global.

Grande parte da força das exportações neste ano foi impulsionada pelo movimento global de expansão da infraestrutura de inteligência artificial.

“As perspectivas para as exportações dependem de quanto tempo durará o boom da IA”, escreveram analistas do Macquarie. Eles esperam que as exportações chinesas acelerem ainda mais no quarto trimestre, antes de começarem a desacelerar a partir do primeiro trimestre de 2027.

articles.title: Trump says FBI probing Nvidia CEO Huang’s affair with alleged spy
articles.summary: US president says he believes CEO Jensen Huang had no knowledge of woman’s alleged work for Chinese intelligence.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump has said the FBI is probing Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with a woman accused of working for Chinese intelligence services.

Speaking at the White House on Monday, Trump said law enforcement had begun inquiries following Huang’s admission that he engaged in an extramarital relationship with a Chinese executive named Alice Huang.

“We’ll look into it. I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else,” Trump told reporters at a news conference. “I think he will be in good shape.”

Trump said Huang told him earlier that he had “absolutely no idea” that the woman was an alleged intelligence agent.

“He said, ‘I had no idea that she was a spy,’ and I really believe him,” Trump said.

Asked by a reporter when he first became aware of concerns about the relationship, Trump said it was “not too long ago”.

“I have been hearing about it and I have been reading a little bit about it over a period of time,” the US president said.

Nvidia, which dominates the market for high-end chips used to power artificial intelligence, did not immediately respond to Al Jazeera’s request for comment.

Nvidia on Sunday announced that it had opened a probe into its CEO’s relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, following media reports that cited US intelligence claiming she worked for China’s Ministry of State Security.

Nvidia’s board of directors said it had no reason to believe that national security or company secrets were compromised, but that an independent inquiry overseen by outside counsel would examine “all available information”.

In a separate statement admitting to an extramarital relationship, Huang apologised to his family, colleagues and shareholders, and pledged to cooperate fully with the board’s inquiry.

Huang’s admission came after the New York Times and the Financial Times last week reported that unnamed US officials had authored a memo alleging that he had been targeted by Alice Huang for intelligence-gathering activities.

China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Monday rejected the allegations, with spokesperson Guo Jiakun saying the reports were “groundless speculation, and a smear against China”.

Alice Huang, who is not related to Jensen Huang, has not publicly commented on the claims.

Nvidia, based in Santa Clara, California, is a critical player in the global AI race, controlling an estimated 80 to 90 percent of the market for graphics processing units (GPUs) used to run frontier models.

Shares of Nvidia, one of the world’s most valuable companies, fell 4.27 percent on Monday to close at $178.67.

articles.title: Oil prices today: Crude edges lower as Donald Trump signals pause in military action against Iran
articles.summary: Oil prices edged lower on Tuesday, extending the previous session's losses, after US President Donald Trump said military action against Iran was not
articles.body: Oil prices edged lower on Tuesday, extending the previous session's losses, after US President Donald Trump said military action against Iran was not necessary “at this point”. His remarks eased concerns over prolonged disruptions to oil supplies from the Middle East.Brent crude futures fell 24 cents, or 0.23%, to $92.33 a barrel by 0102 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures declined 35 cents, or 0.40%, to $86.50 a barrel.Brent had settled 5.85% lower in the previous session after falling to its lowest level since August 31.Trump signals pause in strikes, but Hormuz blockade to continueTrump said on Monday that he planned to hold off on fresh military strikes against Iran for the time being, following appeals from countries in the region. These included an appeal from Qatar's prime minister during talks at the White House.In an interview with Reuters and a subsequent appearance in the White House briefing room, Trump said the US would maintain its naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz for now.“The market continues to prioritise President Trump's more conciliatory tone toward Iran since the midterms,” said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade.He added that attacks on shipping around the Strait of Hormuz were continuing but had not escalated enough to bring a fresh risk premium into the market.However, senior US and Gulf officials have expressed doubts about the possibility of an imminent peace deal between Washington and Tehran.Iranian security council chief Mohsen Rezaei rejected reports of negotiations, saying the US should “stop manufacturing fake news about imaginary talks”.He added that it was “time to surrender to the seven conditions Iran has repeatedly set out”.Opec output rises, Russia-Ukraine talks in focusOn the supply side, oil production by the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (Opec) increased in October, according to a Reuters survey. The rise was led by higher output in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq, despite continued constraints on exports.Elsewhere, Russian and Ukrainian officials were scheduled to meet on Tuesday for two days of US-brokered talks. articles.summary: Southeast Asian economies will require an estimated $7.1 trillion in infrastructure investments by 2040, but the region is facing a substantial funding
articles.body: Southeast Asian economies will require an estimated $7.1 trillion in infrastructure investments by 2040, but the region is facing a substantial funding shortfall, according to a new report released by the asian development bank (ADB) on Tuesday.According to news agency Reuters, the ADB has revised its assessment of infrastructure requirements for the association of southeast asian nations (ASEAN), more than doubling its earlier estimate of $3.15 trillion for the 2016-2030 period.The report highlighted the following key findings:Prioritising essential infrastructure: Governments should focus on projects that strengthen transportation networks, electricity supply and healthcare facilities, the bank said.A significant funding deficit: Existing spending by ASEAN governments is expected to meet only 45% of the total infrastructure requirement, leaving a funding gap of nearly $4 trillion.Need for private investment: With private capital also constrained, the ADB said governments must deploy public funds strategically to attract private investors and establish predictable investment conditions.Electricity and transport dominate requirements: Around half of the region's infrastructure investment needs are linked to electricity, while nearly a third will go towards upgrading transportation systems, including roads, airports and rail networks.You use AI every day. articles.summary: The festive season has brought changes to the regular trading schedule, with Indian stock exchanges observing holidays around Diwali.
articles.body: The festive season has brought changes to the regular trading schedule, with Indian stock exchanges observing holidays around Diwali. After a special Muhurat Trading session on Sunday and a regular trading session on Monday, investors may be looking to resume trading on Tuesday, November 10.According to the 2026 holiday calendar of the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), will remain closed on account of Diwali-Balipratipada. The holiday applies to the equity, equity derivatives and securities lending and borrowing (SLB) segments, among other market segments.Sensex and Nifty ended higher on Monday, recovering after marginally slipping in the special Muhurat trading session on Sunday. The Sensex rose 107.25 points, or 0.13 per cent, to 81,106.65, while the Nifty gained 58.25 points, or 0.23 per cent, to reclaim the 25,000 mark at 25,044.65. Buying in banking and financial stocks, along with a decline in crude oil prices, supported the benchmarks, although losses in IT and metal shares capped gains. Brent crude fell 1.04 per cent to $97.46 per barrel.Also read: Are banks open or closed on November 10, 2026? Check state-wise listAre NSE and BSE closed?Yes. Both the NSE and BSE will remain closed on Tuesday, November 10, for Diwali-Balipratipada.Trading will remain suspended across the equity, equity derivatives and SLB segments. The capital market, derivatives market, electronic gold receipts (EGR) and debt market will also remain closed.The exchanges will resume normal trading on Wednesday, November 11, with the regular equity market session scheduled from 9:15 am to 3:30 pm.Meanwhile, the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) will remain closed during the morning session, from 9 am to 5 pm. However, trading will resume in the evening session from 5 pm to 11:30 pm.The National Commodity and Derivatives Exchange (NCDEX), meanwhile, will remain closed for the entire day.The exchanges have declared November 10 a trading holiday on account of Diwali-Balipratipada, also known as Bali Pratipada. The festival is observed on the day after Diwali and marks the annual return of King Mahabali to his kingdom, according to Hindu mythology.The holiday follows the special Muhurat Trading session held on Sunday, November 8, to mark the beginning of Samvat 2083, the Hindu financial year. The exchanges subsequently conducted a regular trading session on Monday, November 9.After the November 10 closure, the next scheduled trading holiday for the NSE and BSE is November 24, Tuesday, on account of Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev.The exchanges will also remain closed on December 25 for Christmas, according to their 2026 holiday calendars, apart from the regular weekend holidays.You use AI every day.
